# Reins for Hermes Desktop

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/guides/hermes-desktop-plugin.html
Section: Guides

> A Hermes Desktop plugin that makes the Hermes window a surface with three named actions. Built and statically checked, not run in Hermes. Rendered from integrations/hermes-desktop/README.md.

A desktop plugin for Hermes Agent (Nous Research) that makes the Hermes Desktop window a
Reins surface with declared actions. An agent outside Hermes, Claude Code for one, can
then send Hermes a prompt and read the reply, with the Reins consent prompt, indicator,
panel, Pause and Stop in the Hermes window.

**Status: built and statically checked, not run in Hermes.** The plugin builds, and its
own source runs in the repository's tests against a stand-in for Hermes's SDK
(`packages/electron/test/hermes-plugin.test.ts`). The built file passed the import
scanner of Hermes's own plugin loader (`apps/desktop/src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts`)
when that was run over it by hand, outside Hermes. It has not been installed, loaded or
used in a live Hermes Desktop. It was written from the Desktop plugin SDK documentation
in the Hermes repository (`website/docs/developer-guide/desktop-plugin-sdk.md`) at the
version installed in November 2026 (Electron 44.10.2).

The other way to reach Hermes Desktop, with nothing installed into it, is to adopt it
with `reins-electron`: see [docs/ELECTRON.md, section 6](../reference/electron-guide.md#6-claude-controls-hermes).
That way gives an agent the whole Hermes window, every button in it. This plugin gives it
three named actions and nothing else, and is the one to use when the point is to let an
agent talk to Hermes.

## What an agent gets, and what it does not

Hermes is an agent that holds tools: your files, your shell, your accounts. So the
question for this plugin is what one approved attach is worth, and the answer is kept
small on purpose.

| | Risk | |
|---|---|---|
| action `prompt.send {text}` | dangerous | Sends `text` in Hermes's conversation in front, through `host.composer.submit(null, text)`: the same as typing and pressing Enter. You are asked each time and shown the whole prompt. Refused with `E_BUSY` while Hermes is in the middle of a turn there, with `E_NO_TARGET` when Hermes does not say which conversation is in front, and with `E_INTERNAL` when this Hermes gives no sign of whether a turn is under way. |
| action `prompt.draft {text}` | dangerous | Puts `text` in Hermes's message box and sends nothing (`host.composer.setDraft`). You are asked each time as well: the words are then one Enter away from Hermes, in your name. |
| action `reply.read` | safe | Hermes's reply to the caller's own last `prompt.send`: `{ session, text, complete, truncated, at }`. An agent that did not send the prompt gets an empty reply. |
| state `conversation` | | `{ session, busy, awaitingResponse, model }` of Hermes's conversation in front. |

What it does not get:

- **No clicks and no typing.** The plugin's policy grants no `ui` scope, whatever an
  agent asks for at attach. It cannot press Send, and it cannot press the button with
  which you approve a tool call of Hermes.
- **No view of the page.** Nothing of Hermes's interface is exposed (`exposure: 'none'`):
  `reins_observe` returns an empty tree and `reins_read` no text. What an agent learns of
  Hermes is what `reply.read` gives it and what the state `conversation` says.
- **No reply that is another agent's.** The reply is held to the agent whose prompt it
  answers: `reply.read` gives it to that agent and an empty one to any other, and it is
  not a state, because a state is the same for every agent that was allowed to look. It
  is forgotten when that agent's grant ends.
- **No reply from another conversation.** The reply is collected from the gateway events
  `message.start`, `message.delta`, `message.complete` and `message.error`, at most
  16 000 characters, and only from events that name the session the prompt went to. An
  event without a session id, or from a conversation in the background, is not taken for
  the answer. And because the reply is whatever Hermes says next in that conversation,
  `prompt.send` is refused while Hermes is in the middle of a turn there
  (`host.state.busyBySession`, `host.state.busy`, `host.state.awaitingResponse`), and
  also when this Hermes offers none of those signs: otherwise the end of an answer to
  your own message could be read as the answer to the agent's prompt.
- **No prompt you could not read.** A prompt is approved on a card that shows all of it,
  or it is not sent. See below for the limit.
- **No way to act without you, unless you say so.** See the next section.
- **No refusal because you were looking elsewhere.** A card you did not answer waits for
  you in the panel; see "When you are in another window".

The scopes an agent can hold are `observe`, `act`, `show` and `chat`.

## The levels, and letting prompts through without the question

Both writing actions are declared `dangerous`. In Reins that word has one exact
consequence: the level Auto stops asking about sensitive actions and never about
dangerous ones. So this is what each level in the panel of the Hermes window ("AI
connected", Permissions) means for this plugin:

| Level | `prompt.send` and `prompt.draft` | `reply.read` |
|---|---|---|
| Strict | ask you, every time | asks you too |
| Ask, where every agent starts | ask you, every time | runs |
| Auto | ask you, every time. For this plugin Auto is the same as Ask | runs |
| Bypass | run without asking, unseen, at any length up to 8000 characters | runs |

**Bypass is the only level under which a prompt reaches Hermes without you.** The rule
Allow for `prompt.send` or `prompt.draft` does the same for that one action; it can be
set for the same reason Bypass can, and only because Bypass is on offer. Either takes
two steps: you choose it, and then confirm on a step that names the agent and the
actions that will stop asking. While it holds, the indicator in the Hermes window shows
it in red. The level lasts until that agent disconnects or you set it back.

**The rule Allow for `prompt.send` is the easy way, and it is offered where you are
anyway.** There are three places to set it, and it is the same rule in each:

- on the card that lets the agent connect, as a box to tick: "Without asking each time",
  `prompt.send`. Unticked, nothing changes. Ticked, Allow shows a second step that names
  the agent and the action, and the button there sets it;
- on a card that asks about one prompt, as "Always allow", with the same second step;
- in the panel, on the action's row.

On the second step you choose how long: until this agent disconnects, or for fifteen
minutes, after which every prompt asks again. `prompt.draft` is not offered on the
connect card: an unasked draft puts the agent's words into your message box, where one
Enter sends them as yours. You can still set its rule in the panel.

**Prompts that run without a question are counted.** After five of them by one agent in
ten minutes, the next one asks again, with a card that says why and shows the prompt,
whatever waived the question: your rule, or Bypass. Allow on that card starts the count
again. Five is this plugin's choice, well under the twenty of the guarded profile: each
prompt is a turn of Hermes's model, and whatever Hermes does with it.

Know what it means before you do it. From then on every prompt that agent writes goes to
Hermes without you seeing it first, and Hermes acts on a prompt with its own tools, under
whatever Hermes's own approvals are set to. A web page, a document or another agent that
manages to steer the outer agent can then reach those tools through it. Leave the level
at Ask unless you are watching, or unless Hermes itself asks you before it acts.

**A prompt too long to show cannot be approved.** A consent card shows the whole prompt
or the request is refused before you are asked: nobody should approve words they cannot
read. A card holds 2000 characters in all, of which the argument's name and its
quotation marks take 16, and a line break or a quotation mark inside the prompt counts
as two. That leaves about 1,900 characters for a prompt in plain text. A longer one
answers `E_TOO_LARGE` under Strict, Ask and Auto, and nothing is sent. What to do: send
a shorter prompt, or several, one after the other. Under Bypass there is no card, so the
limit there is the action's own, 8000 characters, none of which you see.

## When you are in another window

You drive the outer agent from its own window, and the card comes up in the Hermes
window, which you are not looking at. Before, the request was refused after a minute.
Now:

1. **The card waits for a minute, then the request waits in the panel.** Nothing is
   refused and nothing runs. "Later" on the card does the same at once. The request stays
   in the list for ten minutes.
2. **The agent is told** that its request waits in your window, that nothing ran, and for
   how long it stays there (error `E_WAITING`, with a ticket). The Reins tools say this to
   the model in plain words and tell it not to ask you for the approval in the chat.
3. **The plugin tells you**, with one desktop notification, while the Hermes window is not
   in front: "Hermes Desktop: a request is waiting for you". The words are the plugin's.
   Nothing an agent named or wrote is in them: no agent name, no action, no prompt. The
   notification takes no focus and raises no window. One per stretch: a card that then
   moves to the list does not notify again, and coming to the window ends the stretch. If
   Hermes Desktop does not grant notifications to its page, there is none; the plugin does
   not ask for the permission.
4. **In the Hermes window** the indicator reads "1 waiting". The panel lists the request
   under "Waiting for your answer": the agent, the action, its risk and since when, and
   not the prompt. **Review** opens the card again exactly as it was asked, with the whole
   prompt, and with every rule a card has. Allow there approves it; Deny refuses it;
   **Discard** in the list refuses it without a card.
5. **The agent repeats the request**, and it runs: once. The approval is for that request
   by that agent, word for word; the same ticket with another prompt, or from another
   agent, is a new question. After it ran, the next prompt asks again. An approval you
   gave and the agent has not used yet can be taken back in the list.

A request also stops waiting when its agent disconnects, and when its ten minutes are
over (the agent is told that too). One agent can have three requests waiting, and the
window twelve.

## Two conversations in one window

With the plugin on, the Hermes window holds two conversations. They are not the same and
do not mix:

| | who talks | where it is | how an agent uses it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hermes's own conversation | you and Hermes | the Hermes interface: its message box and transcript | `prompt.send`, `prompt.draft`, `reply.read`, the state `conversation` |
| the Reins chat room | you and the agent that drives Hermes (Claude, say) | the Chat tab of the panel that opens from "AI connected" | `reins_chat` (scope `chat`) |

An agent that calls `prompt.send` puts words into Hermes's message box, and Hermes
answers them. An agent that calls `reins_chat say` talks to you in the panel, and Hermes
never sees it. What you type in the Chat tab goes to the attached agent, not to Hermes;
what you type in Hermes's message box goes to Hermes, and the attached agent does not see
it, since the page is not exposed. The Reins transcript is in a closed shadow root and is
not part of what the plugin exposes either. A message in the Reins chat approves nothing:
"yes, send it" there does not answer the prompt for `prompt.send`.

## Build

The plugin is built with the package: after `npm install` in a checkout of the Reins
repository,

```bash
npm run build
```

writes `dist/hermes-desktop/reins/plugin.js`, about 350 kB: the plugin with the Reins
driver bundled in. Hermes loads a desktop plugin as one module and refuses every import
but `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and React, which is why the driver cannot be loaded from a file
next to it. The build fails if the result imports anything else. The npm package ships
the built file at `node_modules/@offensiveadhd/reins/dist/hermes-desktop/reins/plugin.js`;
the source is `integrations/hermes-desktop/src/plugin.js` in the repository.

## Install (not run)

A desktop plugin is a folder named after its id, holding `plugin.js`, in Hermes's
`desktop-plugins` folder. Hermes watches that folder.

```powershell
# Windows
Copy-Item -Recurse dist\hermes-desktop\reins "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\desktop-plugins\reins"
```

```bash
# macOS, Linux: $HERMES_HOME is ~/.hermes unless you moved it
cp -r dist/hermes-desktop/reins "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/desktop-plugins/reins"
```

Then, in Hermes Desktop, enable "Reins" under Capabilities, Plugins. The plugin declares
`defaultEnabled: false`, so it does nothing until you do.

Start a hub that admits the Hermes window and asks about the two writing actions. The
window is a page loaded from a file, so its origin is `file://`. And a hub under the
plain guarded profile refuses a dangerous action outright (`prompt.send` would answer
`E_DENIED`, "action denied by hub policy"), so the hub needs to be told to ask instead.
[`hub.json`](https://github.com/offensiveadhd/reins/blob/main/integrations/hermes-desktop/hub.json), next to this file and in the npm package, says both:

```bash
npx --no -- reins-hub --config node_modules/@offensiveadhd/reins/integrations/hermes-desktop/hub.json
```

```json
{
  "policy": { "profile": "guarded", "actions": { "prompt.send": "confirm", "prompt.draft": "confirm" } },
  "surfaces": { "origins": ["file://"] }
}
```

The hub prints a warning about `file://`: it is true, see the first limit below. (What
this configuration decides for the plugin's actions is checked in
`packages/electron/test/hermes-plugin.test.ts`; the hub was not run with Hermes
connected.)

## Use (not run)

In the order you and the agent meet it. None of this was run in a live Hermes; every step
is run against the stand-in for Hermes's SDK in `packages/electron/test/hermes-plugin.test.ts`.

```bash
node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" reins_attach '{"reason":"ask Hermes a question"}'
node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" reins_act '{"action":"prompt.send","args":{"text":"Summarise the open pull requests"}}'
node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" reins_act '{"action":"reply.read"}'    # repeat until "complete":true
```

1. **Connect.** `reins_attach` raises a card in the Hermes window. You are there for this
   one: read it, and decide about the box "Without asking each time: `prompt.send`".
   - Left unticked: Allow connects the agent, and every prompt will ask you.
   - Ticked: Allow shows what will run without asking; choose "For 15 minutes" or "Until
     this agent disconnects", and press "Allow with these".
2. **The first prompt.** `reins_act` with `prompt.send`. With the rule it goes to Hermes
   at once. Without it, a card shows the whole prompt.
3. **If you miss the card**, the agent's call does not fail with a refusal: it is told
   that the request waits in your window. You get the notification, find the request
   under "Waiting for your answer", press Review, read the prompt and press Allow. The
   agent calls `reins_act` again with the same arguments, and the prompt is sent. (The
   tool keeps the ticket; an agent on the SDK passes it as `tk`, or lets the SDK wait and
   repeat.)
4. **The reply.** `reins_act` with `reply.read`, until `complete` is true.
5. **After a while.** A fifteen-minute rule ends by itself, and the next prompt asks. And
   the sixth unasked prompt within ten minutes asks whatever the rule says.

With the MCP adapter registered, the same are the tools `reins_attach` and `reins_act`.
`reply.read` answers the session that sent the prompt: read with the same agent.

## Limits, and what is not known

- **`file://` on a socket.** A hub that admits `file://` admits every local HTML file
  opened in a Chromium browser, not only Hermes (docs/SECURITY.md, T57). Run that hub only
  while you use it. Adopting Hermes with `reins-electron` does not have this limit, and
  gives the agent every button in the window in exchange.
- **The hub is unverified to the page.** The plugin holds no surface key, so the prompt,
  the indicator, the panel's confirm step and the Chat tab say "Unverified hub", and
  every attach asks. A key in a plugin would be readable by every other plugin in the
  same page, so none is offered.
- **A plugin is not a boundary.** It runs in Hermes's own page with the app's authority,
  next to every other plugin. Reins protects the person from the agent; it does not
  protect Hermes from its plugins.
- **Not verified in a live Hermes**: that `host.composer.submit(null, text)` returns
  `true` when a conversation is in front; that `host.state.focusedSessionId` names it at
  that moment (without it `prompt.send` refuses); the exact fields of the `message.*`
  events (the plugin reads `payload.text`, as the app's own handler does, and looks for
  the session id under `session_id`, `sessionId` and `payload.session_id`; an event that
  carries none is ignored); that the driver's indicator and panel sit well over Hermes's
  interface; that hot reload disposes the driver (`ctx.onDispose`).
- **Also not verified in a live Hermes**: that Hermes Desktop grants its page the Web
  Notifications API (Electron does by default; an app can refuse it, and then the plugin
  stays silent), and what such a notification looks like on each system.
- **The waiting list needs a hub that speaks protocol 0.2**, which the hub of this
  package does. With an older hub a card nobody answers is refused after a minute, as
  before, and the connect card offers nothing.
- **The hub address is fixed** at `ws://127.0.0.1:7346` in `src/plugin.js`.

# Methods

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/reference/methods.html
Section: Reference

> Every request an agent can send, with its parameters, its result and the scope it needs, and how a surface behaves for each.

## The table

Agent side. All but the first two and `stream.close` take `s`, the surface id.

| method | params | result | scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hub.info` | | `HubInfo` | |
| `surfaces.list` | | `{surfaces}` | |
| `surface.attach` | `scopes, reason?, tk?` | `{grant, surface, manifest}` | |
| `surface.detach` | | `{}` | |
| `observe` | `since?, boxes?` | `Observation` | observe |
| `read` | `h?, max?` | `{text, truncated}` | observe |
| `state.get` | `name?` | `{state}` | observe |
| `sub` / `unsub` | `topics` | `{topics}` now subscribed | observe |
| `act` | `a, args?, tk?` | `{result?, rev}` | act |
| `ui.click` | `h` | `{rev}` | ui |
| `ui.type` | `h, text, clear?, enter?` | `{rev}` | ui |
| `ui.select` | `h, value` | `{rev}` | ui |
| `ui.scroll` | `h?, dx?, dy?, to?` | `{rev}` | ui |
| `ui.key` | `key, h?` | `{rev}` | ui |
| `cursor.move` | `to, ms?, wait?` | `{x, y}` | cursor |
| `cursor.set` | `visible?, label?, color?` | `{}` | cursor |
| `show.toast` | `text, kind?, ms?` | `{}` | show |
| `show.highlight` | `h, label?, ms?` | `{}` | show |
| `show.view` | `view, data?` | `{result?}` | show |
| `show.clear` | | `{}` | show |
| `nav.go` | `url` | `{}` | nav |
| `chat.say` | `text, to?` | `{id}` | chat |
| `chat.read` | `since?, max?` | `{messages, next}` | chat |
| `chat.status` | `state, note?` | `{}` | chat |
| `stream.open` | `kind:"pointer"` | `{ch, credit}` | cursor |
| `stream.close` | `ch` | `{}` | |

A request is `req {id, m, p}` and is answered by exactly one `res`. There are 27 methods in protocol 0.2; on a link that negotiated 0.1 the three `chat.*` methods are not among them ([Protocol versions](./protocol-versions.md)). `act` and `surface.attach` take `tk` (0.2), the ticket of a request that waited for the person and was allowed ([Requests that wait](../concepts/waiting-requests.md)). An unknown method is answered `E_UNKNOWN_METHOD` before any parameter is checked.

## Who answers

The hub answers six methods itself: `hub.info`, `surfaces.list`, `surface.attach`, `surface.detach`, `stream.open` and `stream.close`.

Every other method is forwarded. The hub checks the grant, the scope and the rate limit, strips `s`, and sends the request to the surface with `ag` set to the agent's session id, and `c:1` when the hub policy demands a human confirmation. The surface's answer is relayed back unchanged.

## Read-only methods

`observe`, `read`, `state.get`, `sub`, `unsub` and `chat.read` are the read-only methods. They stay available while the person has paused control and while a consent prompt is up. Every other forwarded method fails with `E_PAUSED` in the first case and `E_BUSY` in the second, with one exception: `chat.say` and `chat.status` are served while control is paused, so that a paused agent can still answer the person. While a prompt is up they fail with `E_BUSY` like the rest.

## Targets

A target is a handle from the tree (`e12`) or a semantic id (`#cart.checkout`). An unknown, detached or unexposed target is `E_NO_TARGET`. `ui.*` never accepts coordinates; `cursor.move` accepts a point `{x, y}` in viewport pixels when `policy.coordinates` is on.

## Scope observe

**`observe`** returns the UI tree: a full snapshot, or a delta when `since` equals the agent's last revision. `boxes: true` adds viewport boxes. See [Observation](../concepts/observation.md).

**`read`** returns the visible text of an element or of the page, at most `max` characters (default 2000, cap 8000). Private and ignored subtrees are left out. Under `annotated` exposure only annotated regions are readable.

**`state.get`** returns the current value of one named piece of state, or of all of them.

**`sub`** and **`unsub`** change which event topics the agent receives, and answer with the topics now subscribed. An agent opts into `ui`, `state`, `user` and `nav`.

## Scope act

**`act`** calls an action the app declared.

- An unknown action is `E_BAD_ARGS`. Args are validated against the action's schema: `E_BAD_ARGS` with the failing path.
- A request without `args` is validated as `{}`, which is also what the handler is given.
- Policy decides by the action's risk and overrides: `deny` is `E_DENIED`; `confirm`, or a request carrying `c:1`, shows a consent prompt, and a refusal is `E_CONSENT`.
- The level and the rules the person set for the agent can add a prompt, waive one, or block the action (`E_CONSENT`, with no prompt). See [Permission levels](../concepts/permission-levels.md).
- Then the handler runs. Its result MUST be JSON and at most 32 KiB.
- The answer is `{result?, rev}`: the handler's result and the tree revision after it ran.

## Scope ui

Synthetic input on exposed elements. Every `ui.*` command waits until the person has stopped using the page, and answers `{rev}`.

**`ui.click`** resolves the handle, scrolls it into view, dispatches pointer and mouse events and the click. Disabled elements fail with `E_NO_TARGET`.

**`ui.type`** focuses the element, optionally clears it, sets the value through the native setter and dispatches `input` and `change`. `enter` then sends Enter and submits the enclosing form. A target that takes no text is `E_BAD_ARGS`; a read-only or disabled one is `E_NO_TARGET`.

**`ui.select`** chooses an option of a `<select>` by value or label.

**`ui.scroll`** scrolls the element or the page by `dx, dy`, to `top` or `bottom`, or brings `h` into `view`.

**`ui.key`** dispatches one key on `h` or the focused element. The keys are `Enter`, `Escape`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Space`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home` and `End`. Tab moves focus as the browser would among exposed elements, and never to a private one.

Every command that synthesises input fails with `E_DENIED` on a private target unless `policy.privateInput`. See [Privacy annotations](../guides/privacy-annotations.md).

## Scope cursor

Visual only: never dispatches input.

**`cursor.move`** animates the virtual cursor to a target or, when `policy.coordinates`, to a point. It answers `{x, y}` when the motion ends, or at once with `wait: false`.

**`cursor.set`** shows or hides the cursor, and sets its label (at most 40 characters) and colour (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`).

**`stream.open`** opens a pointer stream and answers `{ch, credit}`. It fails with `E_DENIED` when `policy.coordinates` is off. **`stream.close`** closes it. See [Cursor and the pointer stream](../concepts/cursor-and-pointer-stream.md).

## Scope show

**`show.toast`**, **`show.highlight`** and **`show.clear`** are overlays the driver renders. Text is always inserted as text. A toast has a `kind`: `info`, `ok` or `warn`.

**`show.view`** validates `data` against the view's schema and calls the app's renderer. A request without `data`, for a view whose schema is an object, is validated as `{}`. This is how data reaches the screen without passing through a model.

## Scope nav

**`nav.go`** resolves `url` against the page. It MUST be same-origin, `http:` or `https:`, with a path under one of `policy.nav`. Otherwise `E_DENIED`. A navigation that reloads the page ends the surface session, and the agent attaches again.

## Scope chat

The room in the page's panel, between the person and the attached agents. See [Chat](../concepts/chat.md).

**`chat.say`** posts a message. `text` is trimmed and is then 1 to 4000 characters; anything else is `E_BAD_ARGS`. `to` is `person`, for the person alone, or names one other agent of the room by its session id. `to: "person"` is always taken. Any other `to` is `E_DENIED` when no other agent hears the speaker, and `E_BAD_ARGS` when it names no other agent that hears the speaker. The answer is the `id` the message has for the agent that said it.

**`chat.read`** returns the messages this agent may read, its own among them, oldest first: without `since` the latest `max` of them, with `since` the first `max` whose `id` is greater. `max` is 20 by default and 50 at most, and an answer holds at most 128 KiB. `next`, passed as `since`, reads on from there.

**`chat.status`** says what the agent is doing: `state` is `idle`, `thinking` or `working`, with a `note` of at most 80 characters. A state that was not renewed for 2 minutes reads `idle` again, and every state is dropped when a consent prompt comes up.

Only `text` and `to` of a `chat.say` are forwarded to the surface. An agent cannot send an event: it hears the room as `evt chat`.

## Ordering

A surface runs commands that change the page one at a time, in arrival order. `observe`, `read`, `state.get` and the three `chat` methods are answered immediately: chat changes the Chat tab and nothing on the page.

## On the other leg

Between the hub and a surface, forwarded methods arrive with the same name and params minus `s`. Five methods exist only on that leg:

| method | params | result |
|---|---|---|
| `attach` | `agent, scopes, reason?, levels?, decisions?, chatRelay?, cred?, v?, tk?` | `{scopes, ttlMs, kept?}`, or `E_WAITING` |
| `detach` | `why`: `agent`, `hub` or `expired` | `{}` |
| `stream.open` | `kind:"pointer", ch` | `{credit}` |
| `stream.close` | `ch` | `{}` |
| `chat.undelivered` | `id` | `{}` |

In `attach`, `levels` is the list of permission levels the hub's policy offers, `decisions` is what the hub's policy decides for each action of the surface's manifest, `chatRelay` is the hub's setting for who hears whom in the chat, and `cred` is the id of the agent's credential, by which a surface knows an agent again whatever its session id or name. In the answer, `kept` is what stays of the person's earlier settings for that agent: the level `strict`, rules `confirm` and `deny`, and scopes switched off. The hub reads nothing else from it, and `surface.attach` hands `kept` on to the agent with the grant. `v` (0.2) is the protocol version the agent's own link speaks, so that a surface puts no request of an agent on 0.1 in its waiting list, and `tk` is a ticket, forwarded as the agent sent it. A request that waits for the person is answered `E_WAITING` with `data: {tk, ms}` instead of a result, and the surface reports the person's answer as `evt user {kind:"answer"}`. See [Grants and scopes](../concepts/grants-and-scopes.md#what-ends-with-a-grant-and-what-stays). `chat.undelivered` tells the surface that the hub did not relay a message of the person to the agent `ag` names; the surface shows it as not delivered.

## For implementers

The method to scope table, the hub methods, the read-only methods and scope intersection are in the test vectors: [`methods.json`](../implementers/vectors/methods.md).

## Further reading

- [Specification, section 9](./specification.md#9-methods): the normative text, with every edge case.
- [Error codes](./error-codes.md)

# Events

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/reference/events.html
Section: Reference

> The event topics, what each carries, who receives it and which need a subscription.

## The frame

Events are `evt {topic, d}`. A surface addresses one agent with `ag`, or omits it to reach every attached agent. The hub adds `s`, the surface the event is about, when it relays.

```json
{"t":"evt","topic":"ui","s":"s1","d":{"rev":14}}
```

## Topics

| topic | payload `d` | sent when | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ui` | `{rev}` | The UI tree changed. At most once per 100 ms. It carries only the new revision: call `observe` for the delta. | `sub`, and the `observe` scope |
| `state` | `{name, patch}` | An exposed piece of app state changed. `patch` is an RFC 7396 merge patch against the value this agent last received. | `sub`, and the `observe` scope |
| `nav` | `{url, title}` | The page navigated. | `sub`, and the `observe` scope |
| `user` | `{kind}`: `override`, `pause` or `resume` | The person used the page while an agent was driving it (`override`), or pressed Pause or Resume. | `sub` |
| `user` | `{kind:"level", level}`, `{kind:"rule", a, d, ms?}`, `{kind:"relay", on}` | The person set something for this one agent in the panel: the level of its grant, a rule for one action (`d` is null when the rule was removed or its time ran out; `ms` on a rule `allow` set for a time says how long it lasts), or whether it hears the other agents in the chat. | nothing |
| `grant` | `{kind}`: `revoked` or `expired` | The grant ended: the person pressed Stop or refused three prompts in a row, or the hub ended it (`revoked`), or the grant reached its expiry or went idle (`expired`). | nothing |
| `grant` | `{kind:"scopes", scopes}` | The person switched scopes of the grant off or back on. `scopes` are those now in force. The grant goes on. | nothing |
| `user` | `{kind:"answer", tk, answer, a?}` | (0.2) The person answered a request of this agent that waited: `answer` is `allow`, `deny` or `expired`, `tk` the ticket, `a` the action's name for an `act` request. Sent with `ag` to that agent alone; an agent on protocol 0.1 is told nothing. See [Requests that wait](../concepts/waiting-requests.md). | nothing |
| `surface` | `{kind, surface}`: `added`, `gone` or `changed` | A surface connected, disconnected, or changed its listing. | nothing |
| `chat` | a message: `{id, from, text, ts, to?}` | Someone said something in the page's chat room that this agent may hear: the person, or another agent where the room relays those. Never the agent's own. | the `chat` scope |

## Subscribing

Agents opt into `ui`, `state`, `user` and `nav` with `sub {topics}`, and out with `unsub`. Both answer with the topics now subscribed. `grant`, `surface` and `chat` events need no subscription, and neither do the `user` events `level`, `rule`, `relay` and `answer`.

```js
await handle.subscribe(['ui', 'state', 'user']);
handle.on('ui', ({ rev }) => {});
handle.on('grant', (e) => {});       // { kind: 'revoked' | 'expired' } or { kind: 'scopes', scopes }
handle.on('user', (e) => {});        // also { kind: 'level', level }, { kind: 'rule', a, d }, { kind: 'relay', on }
handle.on('answer', (e) => {});      // the person answered a request that waited: { tk, answer, a? }
handle.on('chat', (message) => {});  // needs no subscribe
client.on('surface', ({ kind, surface }) => {});
```

## Who gets what

The hub relays an event only to live grants with the scope its topic needs: `ui`, `state` and `nav` need `observe`, and `user` goes to every live grant.

`surface` events come from the hub alone:

- `added` and `gone` go to every agent that may attach to that surface;
- `changed` goes only to agents holding a grant on it.

An agent hears about a surface only if its credential may attach to it. Without a live grant that includes `observe`, the `SurfaceInfo` in the event is reduced: `url` is the origin and `title` is the app's name.

## What a surface may not send

A `grant` event from a surface is acted on by its kind and never relayed as it came: `revoked` ends grants, `scopes` changes the scopes of one grant, and any other kind is dropped. The `user` events `level`, `rule` and `answer` say what the person set, or answered, for one agent: the hub checks and records them, and then tells that agent alone. On a link that negotiated protocol 0.1 the hub sends none of the kinds 0.2 added, and drops those a 0.1 surface could not have sent ([Protocol versions](./protocol-versions.md)). A `surface` event sent by a surface is dropped, as is an event with an unknown topic.

A `chat` event is never broadcast. A surface sends it once for each agent that is to hear the message, and the hub relays it to that grant alone, while the grant holds `chat`, in an event built from the checked fields, with the sender's name as the hub gave it. The hub takes no event from an agent, so an agent cannot send one.

Within a version, receivers ignore unknown event topics.

## State patches

A merge patch cannot express a property whose value is null, so such a property reads as absent. A state that differs from the last one only in null properties, or not at all, produces no event.

## Further reading

- [Observation, handles and deltas](../concepts/observation.md)
- [Human control](../concepts/human-control.md)
- [Specification, section 6](./specification.md#6-requests-responses-events)

# Error codes

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/reference/error-codes.html
Section: Reference

> The complete list of error codes in protocol 0.2, what each means, where the specification uses it, and what E_WAITING carries.

## The codes

A request that fails is answered `res {re, ok:false, e:{code, msg}}`. Error messages are short and safe to show to a model. They never contain stack traces, file paths or secrets.

There are 20 codes, and the list is closed:

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_BAD_FRAME` | malformed frame, unknown frame type, a frame out of place |
| `E_VERSION` | no protocol version in common |
| `E_AUTH` | missing or wrong proof, surface key required, key confirmation failed |
| `E_ORIGIN` | the connection's origin, or `hello.surface.url`, is not allowed for the role; a surface on a socket that takes agents only |
| `E_TOO_LARGE` | a frame, request, manifest, result or set of consent arguments over its limit |
| `E_UNKNOWN_METHOD` | the method does not exist |
| `E_BAD_ARGS` | params fail validation |
| `E_NO_SURFACE` | no such surface id, or a surface the credential may not attach to |
| `E_NOT_ATTACHED` | no live grant for this surface |
| `E_SCOPE` | the grant lacks the method's scope, the person switched that scope off, or no requested scope is permitted |
| `E_DENIED` | policy says no |
| `E_CONSENT` | the person refused or blocked the action, or the prompt timed out |
| `E_WAITING` | 0.2: the request waits for the person's answer and nothing ran; `data` is `{tk, ms}`, the ticket of the request and how long it stays. An agent on 0.1 gets `E_CONSENT` (section 16) |
| `E_PAUSED` | control is paused, the indicator cannot be shown, or the person is using the page |
| `E_RATE` | a rate or admission limit, or a consent cool-off |
| `E_NO_TARGET` | the target is not a live, exposed, enabled element, or is read-only |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | the other side did not answer in time |
| `E_GONE` | the other side disconnected |
| `E_BUSY` | a capacity, a pending attach or consent prompt, a permission that changed while the request waited, or a peer that does not read |
| `E_INTERNAL` | an unexpected failure, the audit log unavailable, a result that is not JSON |

`bye` also takes `OK`. A receiver reads an unknown code in a `res` as `E_INTERNAL` and in a `bye` as `E_GONE`.

An error may carry `data`, a JSON value that goes with its code. `E_WAITING` (0.2) is the one code that does: `data` is `{tk, ms}`, the ticket of a request that waits for the person's answer and how long it stays in their list. Nothing ran. The agent repeats the request with the ticket once the person has allowed it; a 0.2 hub sends `E_WAITING` to an agent on protocol 0.1 as `E_CONSENT`, without its `data`. See [Requests that wait](../concepts/waiting-requests.md).

## Where each is used

From the conformance vectors, with the section of the specification first:

| code | where the specification uses it |
|---|---|
| `E_BAD_FRAME` | 4: invalid JSON, unknown t, missing field |
| `E_VERSION` | 16 no common version |
| `E_AUTH` | 5 failed hello, surface key required, key confirmation failed, transcript not well-formed |
| `E_ORIGIN` | 5 origin not allowed for an agent credential or on the surface allowlist; surface url of another origin; 3 a surface on a socket that takes agents only |
| `E_TOO_LARGE` | 4 oversize frame; 9 act result over 32 KiB; 12 consent arguments too large |
| `E_UNKNOWN_METHOD` | 6 and 16 unknown method |
| `E_BAD_ARGS` | 6 params nested too deeply; 9 unknown action, args fail the schema, a chat text or note out of bounds; 12 a chat `to` that names no other agent that hears the speaker |
| `E_NO_SURFACE` | 6 unknown surface id, or one the credential may not attach to |
| `E_NOT_ATTACHED` | 8 no live grant |
| `E_SCOPE` | 8 empty scope intersection, grant lacks scope, scope switched off by the person |
| `E_DENIED` | 5 manifest pin; 8 attach deny; 9 act deny, private target, nav, stream.open without coordinates; 12 a chat `to` from an agent that no other agent hears |
| `E_CONSENT` | 8 attach refused; 9 act refused; 12 third refusal revokes, the person's rule deny |
| `E_WAITING` | 6 a request that waits for the person's answer (0.2); 16 sent to an agent on 0.1 as E_CONSENT |
| `E_PAUSED` | 9 pause; 12 indicator not usable, the person keeps using the page |
| `E_RATE` | 8 attach burst; 11 pointer rate; 12 cool-off; 13 token buckets and admission |
| `E_NO_TARGET` | 9 disabled, unknown, detached, unexposed or read-only target |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | 6 request timeout |
| `E_GONE` | 6 surface disconnected with requests pending |
| `E_BUSY` | 5 more than 16 pending handshakes; 8 attach in flight, more than 32 grants on a surface; 9 prompt up (chat.say and chat.status included), a permission that changed while the request waited; 12 prompts; 13 capacity, a peer that does not read |
| `E_INTERNAL` | 9 handler threw, result not JSON; 13 audit unavailable |

## Reading them

A few distinctions save time:

- **`E_DENIED` or `E_CONSENT`.** Policy said no, or a person did: on a prompt, or by blocking the action in the panel. `E_DENIED` will not change if you ask again. `E_CONSENT` might, later, and asking again at once after a refused prompt is answered `E_RATE`.
- **`E_RATE` or `E_BUSY`.** Too fast, or no room. Both pass. `E_BUSY` is also the answer while a consent prompt is up, to chat as to everything else, and when a permission changed while the request waited: send it again.
- **`E_NO_SURFACE` or `E_NOT_ATTACHED`.** The surface is not there for you, or it is and you hold no grant on it.
- **`E_SCOPE` or `E_DENIED`.** Your grant does not cover this kind of thing, or the person switched that scope off, or it does and this particular thing is refused.
- **`E_PAUSED`.** Not a refusal of the request: the person holds the reins right now.

[Troubleshooting](../guides/troubleshooting.md) says, for every code, what usually causes it and what to do.

## In the SDK

Every refusal rejects with a `ReinsError`:

```js
import { ReinsError } from '@offensiveadhd/reins';

try {
  await handle.act('order.submit');
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ReinsError) console.log(err.code, err.message);
}
```

An action handler in the app refuses the same way: `throw new ReinsError('E_BAD_ARGS', 'that drink is not in the order')`. Anything else a handler throws reaches the agent as `E_INTERNAL` with a generic message.

## In tool results

The MCP adapter and the shell tools print an error as `error <code>: <message>`. When the message was relayed from a page it is marked `[page data]`, and when it came from a handshake that did not finish, `[unverified hub data]`.

## For implementers

The list is in the test vectors: [`errors.json`](../implementers/vectors/errors.md).

# Policy fields

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/reference/policy-fields.html
Section: Reference

> Every field of a policy, what it controls, who enforces it, and its value in each of the three profiles.

## The shape

A policy is a profile plus overrides. Pass a profile name (`'open'`, `'guarded'`, `'kiosk'`), or an object that names a profile and overrides fields of it. Without `profile` an object starts from `guarded`. Nested objects (`risk`, `rates`, `human`, `consent`) merge one level deep.

An unknown field, or a value of the wrong type, is refused when the policy is resolved.

## Fields

| Field | Type | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `profile` | `open`, `guarded` or `kiosk` | The preset the rest starts from. |
| `scopes` | list of scopes | The ceiling on the scopes a grant may carry. |
| `attach` | decision | How an attach request is decided. |
| `risk` | `{safe, sensitive, dangerous}`, each a decision | The decision per risk tier. |
| `actions` | `{name or prefix.*: decision}` | Per-action overrides. Exact beats prefix, longer prefix beats shorter. |
| `exposure` | `auto`, `annotated` or `none` | Which elements the UI tree exposes. |
| `chatRelay` | `off`, `person` or `on` | Whether the agents in a page's chat room hear each other: never, once the person switches it on, or always. `true` and `false` still read as `on` and `off`. |
| `privateInput` | boolean | May `ui.type` write into private fields (passwords, card numbers, one-time codes). |
| `coordinates` | boolean | May `cursor.move` take raw viewport coordinates, and may a pointer stream open. `ui.*` never takes coordinates. |
| `framed` | boolean | May the driver run in a page that sits inside a frame. |
| `nav` | list of path prefixes | Same-origin path prefixes `nav.go` may open. Empty means navigation is off. |
| `rates` | `{scope: number}` | Requests per second, per agent credential per surface, by scope. Enforced by the hub. |
| `pointerRate` | number | Pointer-stream points per second. Enforced by the hub. |
| `ttlMs` | number | The lifetime of a grant. |
| `idleMs` | number | A grant with no request for this long expires. |
| `human.yieldMs` | number | After real user input, input-synthesising commands wait this long. 0 turns yielding off. |
| `human.pause` | boolean | Show a Pause control. |
| `human.stop` | boolean | Show a Stop control that revokes the grant. |
| `human.levels` | list of levels | The permission levels the person may switch a grant to. `strict` and `ask` are always available, listed or not. |
| `human.panel` | boolean | The indicator opens the panel: levels, per-action rules, scope switches, activity and chat. |
| `consent.timeoutMs` | number | A prompt nobody answers is a refusal after this long. |
| `consent.remember` | `never` or `session` | With `session`, an approved action is not asked again under the same grant. |
| `consent.waitMs` | number | (0.2) How long a request nobody answered in time, or one the person put off with "Later", waits in the panel's list; 0 switches the list off. 10 minutes under `open` and `guarded`, 0 under `kiosk`. |
| `human.offer` | list of action names | (0.2) Up to 8 actions the attach prompt may offer to allow without asking each time, each as an unticked box. None by default. |
| `human.allowMs` | number | (0.2) How long a rule `allow` set "for a time" lasts; 0 means the confirm step offers no time. 15 minutes in every profile. |
| `human.burst` | `{max, perMs}` or `false` | (0.2) How many runs of one action by one agent whose prompt was waived go unasked within `perMs` before the next call asks again. 60 in 10 minutes under `open`, 20 under `guarded`, off under `kiosk`. |

A decision is `allow`, `confirm` or `deny`. The strictness order is allow < confirm < deny, and exposure is ordered the same way: auto < annotated < none. For `chatRelay` the strictest is `off`, then `person`, then `on`. A level is `strict`, `ask`, `auto` or `bypass`.

## The profiles

| Field | `open` | `guarded` | `kiosk` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scopes` | `observe`, `act`, `ui`, `cursor`, `show`, `nav`, `chat` | `observe`, `act`, `ui`, `cursor`, `show`, `nav`, `chat` | `observe`, `act`, `cursor`, `show` |
| `attach` | `allow` | `confirm` | `allow` |
| `risk.safe` | `allow` | `allow` | `allow` |
| `risk.sensitive` | `confirm` | `confirm` | `deny` |
| `risk.dangerous` | `confirm` | `deny` | `deny` |
| `actions` | none | none | none |
| `exposure` | `auto` | `auto` | `annotated` |
| `privateInput` | off | off | off |
| `coordinates` | `true` | `true` | off |
| `framed` | off | off | off |
| `nav` | `/` | `/` | none |
| `chatRelay` | `on` | `person` | `off` |
| `rates.observe` | 30 | 20 | 20 |
| `rates.act` | 30 | 20 | 10 |
| `rates.ui` | 60 | 40 | 0 |
| `rates.cursor` | 120 | 60 | 60 |
| `rates.show` | 30 | 20 | 10 |
| `rates.nav` | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| `rates.chat` | 10 | 5 | 0 |
| `pointerRate` | 4000 | 2000 | 2000 |
| `ttlMs` | 8 h | 2 h | 8 h |
| `idleMs` | 30 min | 15 min | 5 min |
| `human.yieldMs` | 600 ms | 800 ms | 400 ms |
| `human.pause` | `true` | `true` | `true` |
| `human.stop` | `true` | `true` | off |
| `human.levels` | `strict`, `ask`, `auto`, `bypass` | `strict`, `ask`, `auto`, `bypass` | none |
| `human.panel` | `true` | `true` | off |
| `human.offer` | none | none | none |
| `human.allowMs` | 15 min | 15 min | 15 min |
| `human.burst.max` | 60 | 20 | off |
| `human.burst.perMs` | 10 min | 10 min | off |
| `consent.timeoutMs` | 60 s | 60 s | 30 s |
| `consent.remember` | `session` | `never` | `never` |
| `consent.waitMs` | 10 min | 10 min | off |

This table is printed from `POLICY_PRESETS` of the built package (`packages/core/src/protocol.ts`) when the site is built. The specification gives the same table in its own words:

| | `open` | `guarded` | `kiosk` |
|---|---|---|---|
| intended for | local development | a person's own browser | unattended stations |
| attach | allow | confirm | allow, with a provisioned agent |
| safe / sensitive / dangerous | allow / confirm / confirm | allow / confirm / deny | allow / deny / deny |
| scopes | all | all | observe, act, cursor, show |
| exposure | auto | auto | annotated |
| raw coordinates | yes | yes | no |
| a page inside a frame (`framed`) | refused | refused | refused |
| navigation | same origin | same origin | off |
| user controls | pause, stop | pause, stop | pause |
| levels the person may set (`human.levels`; strict and ask are always on offer) | strict, ask, auto, bypass | strict, ask, auto, bypass | strict, ask |
| the indicator opens the panel (`human.panel`) | yes | yes | no |
| agents hear each other in the chat (`chatRelay`) | `on`: always | `person`: once the person switches it on | `off`: never |
| remember approvals (`consent.remember`) | session | never | never |
| `consent.timeoutMs` | 60 s | 60 s | 30 s |
| a request nobody answered waits (`consent.waitMs`, 0.2) | 10 min | 10 min | no |
| a rule `allow` for a time (`human.allowMs`, 0.2) | 15 min | 15 min | 15 min |
| unasked runs of one action before it asks again (`human.burst`, 0.2) | 60 in 10 min | 20 in 10 min | no cap |
| actions offered at attach (`human.offer`, 0.2) | none | none | none |
| `human.yieldMs` | 600 ms | 800 ms | 400 ms |
| grant `ttlMs` / `idleMs` | 8 h / 30 min | 2 h / 15 min | 8 h / 5 min |
| `rates` per second: observe, act, ui, cursor, show, nav, chat | 30, 30, 60, 120, 30, 2, 10 | 20, 20, 40, 60, 20, 1, 5 | 20, 10, 0, 60, 10, 0, 0 |
| `pointerRate` per second | 4000 | 2000 | 2000 |

## Who enforces what

The hub and the surface each hold a policy, and a request has to pass both.

- **The hub** enforces `scopes` (when it intersects an attach, and when the person switches one off), `attach`, the risk decision for `act` (it forwards with `c:1` on `confirm`, and says at attach what it decides for each action), `nav`, `coordinates` for `stream.open`, `rates`, `pointerRate`, `ttlMs` and `idleMs`. It caps `human.levels`: the person is offered `auto` and `bypass` only where both policies list them, and the hub ends a grant whose page reports a level beyond its own list. It enforces its own `chatRelay`.
- **The surface** enforces `scopes`, `attach`, the risk decision and `actions` again, and everything only it can: `exposure`, `privateInput`, `coordinates`, `framed`, `nav`, `human`, `consent` and who hears whom in the chat. The stricter `chatRelay` of the two applies.

A grant's expiry is `min(hub ttl, surface ttl)`.

## Example

```js
const policy = {
  profile: 'guarded',
  scopes: ['observe', 'act', 'cursor', 'show'],   // no synthetic input, no navigation
  actions: { 'order.refund': 'deny' },
  nav: [],
  human: { yieldMs: 1000 },
  consent: { timeoutMs: 30_000 },
};
```

## With the SDK

`resolvePolicy(input)` in `@offensiveadhd/reins/core` returns the validated policy: a deep copy of a preset plus the overrides. `decideAction(policy, { name, risk })` returns the decision for an action, and `stricter(a, b)` the stricter of two decisions. `driver.policy` is the policy a driver runs.

## For implementers

The profile table with its defaults, the override precedence and the strictness order are in the test vectors: [`policy.json`](../implementers/vectors/policy.md).

## Further reading

- [Policy profiles](../concepts/policy-profiles.md)
- [Specification, section 12](./specification.md#12-policy)

# Limits

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/reference/limits.html
Section: Reference

> Every size, time and count the protocol fixes, in one place. Frame sizes, timeouts, capacities, rates and the bounds on prompts and observations.

## The announced limits

The hub announces these in `welcome`, and they can be configured:

| Limit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxText` | 262 144 (256 KiB) | The UTF-8 bytes of one text frame |
| `maxBinary` | 16 384 (16 KiB) | The bytes of one binary frame |
| `heartbeatMs` | 15 000 | Idle time after which a side sends `ping`. A peer silent for 2.5 times this is dropped. |
| `reqTimeoutMs` | 15 000 | How long a request waits for its `res` |
| `consentTimeoutMs` | 60 000 | Extra time the hub allows a request that waits on a consent prompt |

A size in bytes counts the UTF-8 bytes of text. A length in characters counts UTF-16 code units unless code points are named. A size limit applies to a frame after its seal is removed.

## By topic

**Connecting.** Default port 7346. Nonces and secrets are 32 random bytes. Keys shorter than 32 characters are rejected. A peer has 5 s to send `hello`, and 5 s for key confirmation. A failed proof is answered after 200 ms, doubling up to 3 s, counting failures in the last minute. At most 16 handshakes pending. Before authentication the hub holds at most 16 messages and 64 KiB from a connection.

**Links.** A link queues at most 4096 inbound messages and 16 MiB. A peer whose send buffer at the hub holds more than max(8 MiB, 4 × `maxText`) is closed.

**Manifest.** At most 64 KiB, 256 actions and 64 views. Names are at most 64 characters. Canonical JSON nests at most 100 levels deep.

**Results and observations.** An action result is at most 32 KiB. Names are cut to 120 characters and values to 200. `read` returns 2000 characters by default and 8000 at most. A cursor label is at most 40 characters, an agent's display name 64 code points. `evt ui` is sent at most once per 100 ms.

**Consent.** One pending prompt per agent, four in total. Arguments on a card: at most 40 keys and items in total, nesting of 4, 2000 code points. Allow arms after 500 ms. A key answers a prompt no sooner than 500 ms after the prompt appeared or moved, after the focus landed on the button and after any other key, and no sooner than 3 s after the last key that types. At most two combining marks in a row are shown as they are. A cool-off of 2 s doubling to 60 s after a refusal; three refusals in a row revoke the grant. A withdrawn prompt shows its notice for 1.5 s. A `ui.*` command gives up after the person has kept using the page for 5 s.

**Requests that wait (0.2).** A request waits `consent.waitMs`, 10 minutes under `open` and `guarded`, from when it joined the list. The list holds 3 requests of one agent and 12 in all. A ticket is 1 to 32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` with at least 96 bits from a CSPRNG (the reference driver: 22 characters); the hub keeps at most 3 tickets of one session on one surface and 16 in all, each for `ms` plus `reqTimeoutMs`, and answers `E_BUSY` over that. An attach prompt offers at most 8 actions (`human.offer`). A rule `allow` for a time lasts `human.allowMs`, 15 minutes, and a rule's `ms` on the wire is at most a day. `human.burst`: 60 unasked runs of one action in 10 minutes under `open`, 20 under `guarded`. The notice after a refusal stays 8 s. The SDK waits for the person's answer up to ten minutes by default; a tool's `wait` is at most 150 s.

**Grants.** A burst of 3 attaches per credential and surface, then one every 2 s. A surface holds at most 32 grants. Lifetimes come from the policy: see [Policy fields](./policy-fields.md).

**What the person sets.** A confirm step arms after 500 ms. More than 20 changes of what the person set within one second end the grant. The activity list holds the last 50 commands.

**Chat.** A message is 1 to 4000 characters after trimming, a status note at most 80. A status reads `idle` again after 2 minutes. The room keeps the last 200 messages. `chat.read` returns 20 messages by default, 50 at most, 128 KiB at most. The hub relays the person's messages to one agent at 5 a second after a burst of 10. `reins_chat wait` lasts 90 s by default and 150 s at most; the adapter keeps 100 unread messages and hands over 20 at a time. `chat-serve` gives one run 120 s by default and reads 64 KiB of its output.

**Pointer streams.** An initial credit of 512 points. At most 2729 points in a frame. Credit comes back once a quarter of the window is consumed. Droppable frames may be dropped above 256 KiB of surface backlog, and a stream is closed above 1 MiB. Playback speeds up above 120 ms of lag, to 4 times at 600 ms. A glide takes between 120 and 900 ms.

**The hub.** 64 surfaces, 32 agents, 4 sessions per credential, 8 streams per agent. `hub.info` and `surfaces.list`: 10 a second, burst 20. Surface admission: 2 a second per origin. Agent admission: 2 a second per credential, burst 20.

**The audit log.** At most 1000 records waiting before the hub fails closed. At most 20 refusal records per second per connection.

**The page.** Commands run within a budget of 6 ms per animation frame.

**Shell sessions.** A session ends after 30 minutes without a call.

# CLI: reins-hub, reins, reins-mcp, reins-tools, reins-electron

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/reference/cli.html
Section: Reference

> The commands the package installs, with the help text each prints. The hub, the agent command, the MCP adapter, the shell tools and the command that adopts an Electron app.

## Running them

The package installs 5 commands. Run them as `npx --no -- <command>` in the project that installed the package:

```bash
npx --no -- reins-hub --profile guarded --allow-origin http://localhost:5173
```

The package is not on the npm registry, and `reins-mcp` there is the name of an unrelated package: in a folder that does not have this one, a plain `npx reins-mcp` offers to install that package instead, and installs it without asking when there is no terminal. With `--no`, npx runs what is installed or stops. The `--` has to follow it: without it npx keeps the options written after the command name for itself.

The help texts below are printed by the commands themselves when this site is built.

## reins-hub

The loopback WebSocket hub.

```text
usage: reins-hub [--port 7346] [--profile open|guarded|kiosk] [--allow-origin <origin>]...
                 [--config hub.json] [--token-file <path>] [--audit <path>] [--audit-key-file <path>]
                 [--surface-key <appId>=<path>]... [--require-key] [--no-announce]
                 [--agent <kid>=<path>]... [--no-surface-sockets]

--agent adds a credential of its own for one agent, with its key in that file (created
when missing): the agent then starts with --kid <kid> --token-file <path>. The first
--agent replaces the default token file; --token-file, when given too, stays the
credential "default".
--no-surface-sockets makes the socket take agents only, for a hub whose pages are all
linked in-process (an Electron app's main process).

A running hub announces itself in the user's Reins folder (~/.reins, or REINS_HOME) and
leaves a launcher there, so an agent on this machine can reach it from a shell:
  node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" reins_attach
--no-announce writes neither.
```

- **Profiles and origins.** `guarded` and `kiosk` need at least one `--allow-origin`. `open` admits `http://localhost:*` and `http://127.0.0.1:*` when none is given. An origin entry is an exact origin, `scheme://host:*` for any port, or `*`.
- **The token.** With no agent configured the hub creates one credential (`kid` `default`) and writes the secret to the token file, by default `.reins/token`. The hub prints file paths, never secrets.
- **Secret files.** A secret file that does not exist is created with a random key. An existing one is refused on POSIX if group or others have any permission on it, and restricted again at start on Windows. A failure to restrict stops the hub.
- **Surface keys.** `--surface-key <appId>=<path>` once per app; `--require-key` refuses every surface without one. See [Surface keys](../guides/surface-keys.md).
- **The audit log.** `--audit <path>` writes one JSON record per line and keeps the chain's head in `<path>.head`. `--audit-key-file` keys the chain. See [The audit log](../concepts/audit-log.md).
- **A credential each.** `--agent <kid>=<path>` adds a credential with that `kid` whose key is in that file, created like any secret file when it is missing. With it and without `--token-file` there is no credential `default`: an agent names its own with `--kid`.
- **`--no-surface-sockets`** makes the socket take agents only, for a hub whose pages are all linked in-process, as in an Electron app's main process.
- **Origins that many pages share.** The hub warns at start when its socket admits `file://` or `null` without requiring a surface key.
- **`--config hub.json`** holds what flags cannot say: agent credentials with caps, a whole policy object, limits and capacities. A malformed configuration stops the hub with "invalid configuration ...".
- **The Reins folder.** Once it listens, the hub announces itself in `~/.reins` and writes the launcher there. `--no-announce` writes neither.

It exits with code 2 on a bad command line or a configuration it refuses.

## reins

The agent command: one request per run.

```text
usage: reins <command> [options]

commands:
  surfaces                    list connected surfaces (JSON)
  card                        print the prompt card
  observe                     print the UI tree
  act <name> [json-args]      call an app action
  click <target>              click an element
  type <target> <text>        type into an element
  move <target>               move the cursor to an element (or x,y)
  toast <text>                show a toast

options:
  --url <ws url>        hub URL (default ws://127.0.0.1:7346)
  --surface <id>        surface id (default: the only surface)
  --token-file <path>   file holding the key (default: the one the running hub announced)
  --name <agent name>   name shown to the user
  --kid <id>            the credential to authenticate as (default "default"); its key
                        is the one in --token-file
  --wait <ms>           when the person puts the request off and it waits in their window,
                        wait at most this long for their answer (default: 10 minutes, or as
                        long as it waits if that is shorter)
  --no-wait             report a waiting request at once instead
```

Each run connects, attaches with the one scope the command needs, does its work and detaches. `surfaces` does not attach. `--kid` names the credential to authenticate as. The command prints text from a page or the hub with every control character other than tab and line feed escaped as `\xNN`, so page content cannot drive your terminal.

A target is a handle, a semantic id such as `#menu.latte`, or for `move` a point written `x,y`.

## reins-mcp

The stdio MCP adapter.

```text
usage: reins-mcp [options]

options:
  --url <ws url>        hub URL (default ws://127.0.0.1:7346)
  --token-file <path>   file holding the key (default: the one the running hub
                        announced); give the full path, because a harness starts
                        this command in the folder its session is in
  --name <agent name>   name shown to the user (default mcp-agent)
  --kid <id>            the credential to authenticate as (default "default"); its key
                        is the one in --token-file
  --scopes <a,b,c>      scopes to request (observe, act, ui, cursor, show, nav, chat)
  --data-dir <dir>      directory reins_show may read JSON files from
```

It is started by an agent harness, not by hand. See [Use it from Claude Code and other MCP harnesses](../start/mcp.md).

## reins-tools

The same 10 tools as commands, for an agent that has a shell and no MCP registration, and the commands that make a machine ready.

```text
usage: reins-tools <tool> [arguments] [options]
       reins-tools up --allow-origin <origin>... | status | stop | down | setup
       reins-tools chat-serve [options] --exec <command> [args...]

tools, the same ten the MCP adapter has (the reins_ prefix may be left out):
  reins_surfaces   list the pages connected to the hub
  reins_attach     call first: asks the person on the page, returns the app's prompt card
  reins_observe    the page as a compact tree, then only what changed
  reins_read       text the tree leaves out: of an element, a region or the page; app state
  reins_act        call an action the app exposes
  reins_ui         click, type, select, scroll, key
  reins_cursor     move, show or hide the agent cursor
  reins_show       toast, highlight, app view, clear
  reins_chat       talk with the person in the page's Chat tab: wait, read, say, status
  reins_batch      up to 20 steps in one call

arguments: the tool's arguments as one JSON object, given as
  '{"action":"cart.add"}'   one argument in single quotes (bash, zsh, PowerShell 7.3+)
  -                         read from standard input (any shell; in Windows PowerShell:
                            '{"action":"cart.add"}' | reins-tools reins_act -)
  @args.json                read from a file

commands:
  up       start a hub in the background unless one is running; --allow-origin names the
           page's origin, --profile open|guarded|kiosk (default guarded), --port
  status   what is running: the hub, this session, the launcher
  stop     end this session; the page shows the agent has left
  down     stop a hub that `up` started
  setup    write the launcher: node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" <tool>
  mcp      be the stdio MCP adapter, for a harness that wants the tools registered:
           claude mcp add --scope user reins node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" mcp
  chat-serve --exec <command> [args...]
           answer the person's chat messages with a program: each message goes to one
           run of the command on standard input, behind a line that says who wrote it,
           on lines starting "| ", and what the command prints is the reply. Whoever
           types in the page's Chat tab decides what the command is given, and the
           command runs here as you: read integrations/chat-serve/README.md first.
           The command is run without a shell, and everything after --exec is its own.
           A command named without a path is looked for in the folders of PATH, never
           in the working directory, and the runner says which file it runs.
           --timeout-ms <n> ends a run that takes longer, with what it started
           (default 120000); --surface <id> names the page; --once stops
           after one answer; --preface <file> puts that file's text in front of each
           message; --wait-ms <n> is how long one wait lasts (default 60000);
           --allow-unverified serves a page that did not prove its app key to the hub:
           any program on this computer can be such a page and write as the person

options:
  --url <ws url>        hub URL (default ws://127.0.0.1:7346)
  --session <id>        tell two agent sessions on one hub apart (default default)
  --name <agent name>   name shown to the person; taken when the session starts
  --token-file <path>   file holding the key (default: the one the running hub announced)
  --kid <id>            the credential the session authenticates as (default "default"),
                        with its key in --token-file; taken when the session starts
  --scopes <a,b,c>      scopes the session may request (observe, act, ui, cursor, show, nav, chat)
  --data-dir <dir>      directory reins_show may read JSON files from

--name, --kid, --token-file, --scopes and --data-dir are taken when a session starts.
On a session that already runs, another value is refused: stop it first.

Nothing is registered and no session needs a restart: a hub that is running has
announced itself in the user's Reins folder (~/.reins, or REINS_HOME).
```

The launcher in the Reins folder runs this command: `node "$HOME/.reins/reins.mjs" <tool>` is `reins-tools <tool>` of the installation that wrote the launcher. Exit code 0 with the tool's text on standard output; 1 with the error text on standard error; 2 for a command line that is not understood. See [Shell tools with nothing registered](../start/shell-tools.md).

`chat-serve` answers the person's chat messages with a program: one run of the command for each message, the message on standard input, no shell. Whoever types in the page's Chat tab decides what the command is given, and the command runs as you: read [Serve chat from any command-line agent](../guides/chat-serve.md) first.

## reins-electron

Loads the driver into the pages of an Electron app that was not built for Reins, through the app's debugging connection.

```text
usage: reins-electron [options] -- <electron app executable> [its arguments...]
       reins-electron [options] --attach <port | host:port | ws url>

Loads the Reins driver into the pages of an Electron app that was not built for Reins,
through the app's debugging connection. An agent can then attach to it under the guarded
profile: the person is asked in the app's window first, and sees and can stop the agent.

Whoever holds a debugging connection controls the app completely. Use this with apps you
would let this program control, and read docs/ELECTRON.md before using --debug-port.

launch (the default): the app is started with --remote-debugging-pipe, so no port is
opened, nobody else can use the debugging connection, and the app ends when this
command ends, however it ends
  --debug-port <n>        start it with --remote-debugging-port=<n> instead: a loopback
                          port that any program on this machine can connect to. The
                          app is whatever browser answers on that port, also when the
                          executable was only a starter; this command closes it over
                          the port when it ends, and a small watcher process does when
                          the command is killed

attach
  --attach <where>        an app already started with --remote-debugging-port=<n>;
                          only a loopback address is accepted

With a debugging port (--debug-port, --attach) other programs can use the debugging
connection too, type and press in the app, and speak to its pages. Pages adopted that
way are therefore never listed as verified, and their prompts say "Unverified hub".

the hub (by default one is hosted here; the pages reach it through the debugging
connection, and its socket takes agents only)
  --port <n>              port of the hosted hub (default 7346)
  --token-file <path>     its agent token (default .reins/token)
  --allow-origin <origin> page origin to adopt, repeatable (default: the origin of the
                          first page the app shows, such as file://)
  --no-announce           do not announce the hub or leave the launcher in ~/.reins
  --hub <ws url>          use a hub that is already running instead, on a loopback
                          address; it has to admit the app's origin. Without
                          --surface-key-file the pages cannot tell that hub from
                          another program, and the app's own scripts can register
                          there under the same origin
  --transport <how>       with --hub: auto (default: the page opens the socket, and the
                          debugging connection carries the frames when it may not),
                          ws, or bridge
  --surface-key-file <p>  with --hub: the surface key that hub holds for --app-id.
                          Not with a debugging port: the key would be readable
                          through it

what an agent may be given (the pages run under the guarded profile)
  --levels <a,b>          permission levels the person may set in the panel beyond
                          Strict and Ask, which only tighten: auto, bypass (default
                          none; a level decides declared actions, and an adopted app
                          declares none)
  --scopes <a,b,c>        scopes an agent may be granted (default observe, act, ui, cursor, show, nav, chat)

the app
  --app-id <id>           id the surface gives itself (default: from the executable's name)
  --app-name <name>       name shown to agents and in the prompt card
  --match <origin|url>    adopt only documents of this origin (http://127.0.0.1:9120,
                          app://notes), or whose URL is this one or lies under it
                          (file:///C:/app/). Both sides are read as URLs; query and
                          fragment are left out. Not a substring: a document elsewhere
                          that repeats the text does not match
  --bundle <path>         the page bundle (default: reins-adopt.iife.js of this package)
```

Whoever holds a debugging connection controls the app completely, and an agent that is allowed to attach to an adopted app can press anything in its window. See [Adopt an Electron app](../guides/adopting-an-electron-app.md).

## Environment

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `REINS_TOKEN` | the agent SDK and everything built on it | The agent's key itself. |
| `REINS_TOKEN_FILE` | the same | A file that holds the key. |
| `REINS_HOME` | the hub, the SDK, the shell tools | The Reins folder, in place of `.reins` in the home folder. |

## In a checkout of the repository

The repository's `package.json` has scripts for the demo: `npm run demo:hub` (a hub with the open profile, a surface key for the demo app and a keyed audit log under `.reins/`), `npm run demo` (the demo page) and `npm run demo:agent` (the scripted agent). See the [Quickstart](../start/quickstart.md).
