| `E_GONE ... no Reins preload script` from `electronLink()` | the window has no preload, or another one | set `webPreferences.preload` to `preloadPath`, or call `exposeReins` in yours |
| `E_DENIED ... Reins needs contextIsolation: true` | the window was created with `contextIsolation: false` | leave it on: it is Electron's default |
| `E_DENIED ... not registered for Reins` | `allow()` was not called for this window | `reins.allow(win, { url })` before the page loads |
| `E_DENIED ... not the one the window was registered for` | the window shows another page than the URL given to `allow()`, or shows a file and was given none | register the page's own URL; for several pages, a list or a function |
| `E_TIMEOUT` from `electronLink()` | the window is not shown: its link waits until it is | show the window, pass a longer `timeoutMs`, or register it with `{ hidden: true }` |
| `E_DENIED ... only the top-level page` | the driver runs inside an `<iframe>` | run it in the window's own page |
| `E_DENIED ... this kind of page` | a `<webview>` guest, an offscreen or background page | section 1 |
| `connect()` rejects with `E_ORIGIN` | the broker's `surfaces.origins` does not name the page's origin | run the probe of section 2 and list what it prints |
| the surface vanishes after a reload | a port ends with its document | nothing: the new page connects again, attach again |
| `reins-electron`: "did not answer on its debugging connection" | the app is already running, refuses the switch, or the executable is a launcher | section 3, "Apps that refuse" |
| `reins-electron`: "not adopted: a page of origin ..." | a page of another origin than the first, or one `--match` does not cover | add `--allow-origin <origin>` for it |
| `reins-electron`: "the app shows pages of more than one origin" | the app's first windows have different origins, and none was named | name the ones to adopt with `--allow-origin` |
| `reins-electron`: "a page of the web site ... is not adopted" | the app shows a site from another machine, and none was named | `--allow-origin <that origin>`, if that site is what you mean to adopt |
| `reins-electron`: "--match: cannot read ... as a URL" | `--match` takes an origin or a URL, not a piece of text | `--match http://127.0.0.1:9120`, `--match file:///C:/app/` |
| `reins-electron`: "a debugging port already answers at 127.0.0.1:..." | another app has that port | another port for `--debug-port`, or `--attach` to adopt the app that is there |
| `reins-electron`: "WARNING: the app is STILL RUNNING and its debugging port ... is STILL OPEN" | the app did not close when asked over its port | end the app yourself: until then any local program controls it |
| `reins-electron`: "--surface-key-file does not go with a debugging port" | a key in a page behind a port can be read through the port | start the app with the pipe (no `--debug-port`, no `--attach`) |
| `E_DENIED ... in no window that is shown` from `electronLink()` | a view registered by its `webContents` is in no window | add the view to a window before its page asks, or register it with `{ hidden: true }` |
| `reins-electron`: "a page with an opaque origin (null) is not adopted" | the page is on a scheme the app did not register as standard, or a `data:` page | `--allow-origin null`, knowing that it adopts every such page of the app |
| `reins-electron`: "cannot start the hub: port 7346 is in use" | a hub is already running there | join it with `--hub ws://127.0.0.1:7346`, or host another with `--port` |
| `reins-electron`: "--hub: refusing the hub at ..." | the hub URL is not on a loopback address | a hub listens on loopback only |
| a page says "offline: no hub answered" with `--hub` | no hub at that URL, or it does not admit the page's origin | start it with `--allow-origin` for the origin `reins-electron` prints |
| an agent's call answers `E_WAITING` | nobody answered the card within a minute, or the person pressed Later: the request waits in the window | answer it in the panel under "Waiting for your answer"; the agent repeats the same call |
| the connect card offers nothing to tick | the app's policy names no `human.offer`, the hub offers no level that would waive that action's prompt, the hub speaks protocol 0.1, or you set that agent to Strict before | sections 4 and 6.1 |
| no taskbar flash while a request waits | `attention` was not passed to `reinsMain`, the page does not call `electronAttention(driver)`, or the window has the focus | section 1 |
| no notification from the Hermes plugin | the Hermes window has the focus, or Hermes Desktop does not grant its page notifications | open the Hermes window: the indicator and the panel show what waits |
| the prompt says "Unverified hub" | the page reached a hub by socket and holds no key, or the app was adopted through a debugging port | expected with `--hub` and no key, and with `--attach` or `--debug-port`; use the pipe and the hosted hub, or the pipe and a surface key |
| `chat-serve` refuses an adopted page as not verified | the app was adopted through a debugging port | adopt it over the pipe, or pass `--allow-unverified` knowing what it accepts ([CHAT.md](./chat-guide.md)) |
| `prompt.send` answers `E_DENIED ... denied by hub policy` (Hermes plugin) | the hub runs the plain guarded profile, which refuses dangerous actions | start it with `integrations/hermes-desktop/hub.json` (6.1, step 4) |
| `prompt.send` answers `E_TOO_LARGE` (Hermes plugin) | the prompt does not fit on a consent card | a prompt under about 1,900 characters, or several |
| a page says "stopped: the command that adopted this app is gone" | the command was killed, or was not heard for 10 s and did not answer for 5 s more | start `reins-electron` again |
| the panel of an adopted app offers no Auto | started without `--levels` | section 4; it changes nothing an agent can do there |
| Auto or Bypass you set is gone | the agent reconnected, or the window reloaded: what loosens lasts for one grant. Strict and your Ask and Block rules stay until the window reloads | set it again |
| `reins_observe` does not show the reply or a paragraph | the tree lists controls, not running text | `reins_read`, with the handle of the element or region |
| `reins_read` ends with "cut at 2000 characters" | one call returns 2000 characters by default | pass `"max"` up to 8000, or a narrower `target` |
| `reins_chat` answers `E_SCOPE` | the grant has no `chat` (started with `--scopes`), or the person switched it off | attach with `chat`; ask the person |
| `reins_chat` answers `E_BUSY` | a consent prompt is up in the window | wait for the call that raised it to return |
| one agent does not hear the other | the person has not switched "Agents can hear each other" on | section 7.3 |
| `E_AUTH` with `--kid` | the key in `--token-file` is not that credential's | pass the file the hub printed for that `kid` |
| `nav.go` answers `E_DENIED` | it takes `http(s)` pages only | navigate with an app action (section 1) |
| the first `electron` run downloads for a while | Electron fetches its binary on first use | wait; about 160 MB, 360 MB unpacked |
| the app starts and nothing else happens (ESM main) | a top-level `await app.whenReady()` | `app.whenReady().then(main)` |

## 10. What was tested

`npm run test:electron` runs [`scripts/smoke-electron.mjs`](https://github.com/offensiveadhd/reins/blob/main/scripts/smoke-electron.mjs)
against the example app with a real Electron. It is not part of `npm test`, and the
repository never installs Electron by itself:

```bash
cd examples/electron && npm install && cd ../..
npm run build
npm run test:electron
npm run test:electron -- builtin adopt-pipe                      # only these scenarios
ELECTRON_BIN=/path/to/another/electron npm run test:electron     # the same checks on another build
```

It needs a person: to press Allow, to open the panel, to choose a level, to type in the
chat. [`scripts/smoke/electron-person.cjs`](https://github.com/offensiveadhd/reins/blob/main/scripts/smoke/electron-person.cjs) plays
one inside the app. It finds the prompt and the panel through the accessibility tree and
uses real mouse and keyboard input, and it prints what each prompt and each confirm step
said. Where a consent card is taller than the window, the card says "Scroll to the end to
review everything before allowing" and its Allow waits for that; the person then turns
the mouse wheel over the card until the hint is gone, says in its log that it scrolled,
and presses. No model is called anywhere. The script's first lines name the Electron binary and
print its Electron, Chrome and Node versions, so a run says what it ran with.

108 checks, all passing on Windows 11 with Electron 45.4.1 (Chrome 156.0.8078.100, Node
24.22.3), the five of `waiting` among them. The run before the waiting list existed passed
its 103 checks with Electron 44.10.2 (Chrome 152.0.7977.169, Node 24.22.2) as well, the
runtime Hermes Desktop ships, by setting `ELECTRON_BIN` to its `electron.exe`; this one
was not repeated with it. The check sends real input to real windows: on a machine that
is busy with other work, or whose display is off or locked, the person's clicks can go
unanswered and attaches then fail on time. Run it on a machine that is doing nothing
else, with the screen on. Its last line says whether every check passed, a failed attach prints
what the person at the window saw and did, and `REINS_SMOKE_VERBOSE=1` echoes
everything the person says as it happens.

| Scenario | What is checked |
|---|---|
| `origins` | the `Origin` header, `location.origin` and `mainFrame.origin` of a file, a standard scheme, a plain scheme and loopback http; the header and `self.origin` of a sandboxed frame |
| `builtin` | the window is a surface; attach asks and is not marked unverified; a safe action; typing and a click; a sensitive action whose prompt names it; a dangerous action refused; the panel opens on a click; Auto through the confirm step, after which the sensitive action runs unasked and the dangerous one is still refused; the chat, both directions; the socket refuses `Origin: app://notes`; a reload, after which the grant is at Ask again |
| `waiting` | the example with a person who is somewhere else: the connect card offers `notes.publish`, and ticked it runs with no card after a second step that names it; a card the person puts off gives the agent `E_WAITING` with a ticket and runs nothing; the indicator and the panel's "Waiting for your answer" list it without arguments; Review and Allow approve it, the agent is told, its repeat runs the action once and the next call asks again; with the window out of front a card makes the app call `flashFrame(true)` once without taking the focus, and it is stopped when the person comes back or answers |
| `builtin-file` | the same app from `file://`: surface, attach, actions; the page cannot navigate its window to another file; another local file loaded into the window gets no link |
| `adopt-pipe` | starts with a pipe and no port; surface; consent; UI tree, typing, a click; the hub lists the page as verified; the page's scripts see nothing of the driver; the panel offers Strict and Ask only; a scope switched off (`E_SCOPE`) and on; the chat, both directions; a reload; a second window; the app ends with the command |
| `adopt-levels` | `--levels auto`: the panel offers Auto too and no Bypass; Auto through the confirm step, which says no action is affected; the agent is told |
| `adopt-relay` | two agents on an adopted page: before the person says so, one does not hear the other; after the person switches "Agents can hear each other" on, through its confirm step, it does |
| `adopt-stop` | attached to a running app and joined to a hub over the page's own socket: a clean stop ends the driver at once and for good; a killed command is noticed by the page, which stops by itself; the same after a script in the page's own world cleared every timer id of the document, and an agent that comes in between gets nothing done |
| `adopt-hub`, `adopt-hub-open` | a hub elsewhere: frames over the debugging connection under `connect-src 'none'`, over the page's own socket without it; the command warns that it has no surface key; the prompt and the indicator say the hub is unverified |
| `adopt-port` | attach to a running app with a debugging port; the prompt and the indicator say "Unverified hub", and the hub lists the page as not verified; in a window made too low for the consent card, Allow does nothing until the card was scrolled to its end, and attaches once it was; the app stays up afterwards |
| `windows` | a window registered with its URL gets a port; a file window without a URL, or registered for another file, gets none; without context isolation the preload refuses and both sides are told; without the sandbox it works; a hidden window gets its link when shown, or at once with `hidden: true`; a view registered by its `webContents` gets none while its window is hidden, one when it is shown, and none in no window; an offscreen page gets none |
| `lifetime` | closing the debugging pipe alone ends the app; an app started with `--debug-port` ends with a killed command; when the executable is only a starter, the command stays with the app behind the port and closes it over the port, stopped or killed; an app that starts itself again is not left behind with its port open |
| `tools-adopted` | the commands of 6.2 with the launcher's shell tools: `reins_attach`, `reins_observe`, `reins_ui`, `reins_read` |
| `tools-together` | the situation of section 7 with two shell sessions: both attach, `chat-serve` answers for one with a stand-in command, each hears the person and the other, the person disconnects one |
| `two-agents` | `examples/electron/two-agents.mjs`: the room, relay, no approval by chat, pause, a level for one agent, a scope switch for one agent, Disconnect, Stop |
| `refusals` | a debugging port that is not on loopback; a window with `devTools: false` (adopted all the same) |

Without Electron, the same code is covered by the conformance suite: the `OR-` and `EL-`
requirements, with stand-ins for Electron, and `MCP-6` for `reins_read`. That is where
frames inside a page, `<webview>` guests, background pages and a fenced frame are
checked; none of those four was seen in a real Electron. There, too, are the lease with
every timer dead (`EL-15`), what a debugging port changes (`EL-16`), the command and its
watcher against a stand-in for a debugging port (`EL-17`) and `--match` (`EL-18`). How the
origin is taken from the first pages is covered by unit tests only. The Hermes plugin's
source runs against a stand-in for Hermes's SDK in
`packages/electron/test/hermes-plugin.test.ts`: the levels, a prompt too long for a card,
whose reply it is, and what the hub configuration of 6.1 decides.
The hub flags `--agent` and `--no-surface-sockets`, the hub's warning about `file://`, and
the launcher's `--kid` are run from the installed package by `npm run test:package`.

Not tested: macOS and Linux; a packaged app; Hermes Desktop itself, in any way; a Claude
Code session; any model; Chrome; a surface key with `reins-electron --hub`;
`session.registerPreloadScript`; a `<webview>` or a fenced frame in a real Electron.

# Writing another implementation

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/writing-an-implementation.html
Section: Implementers

> What it takes to implement Reins in another language or runtime. What the contract is, what has to match exactly, and how the vectors and the conformance suite tell you that you got it right.

## The contract

Reins is a protocol first. The reference implementation is TypeScript, and nothing in the protocol depends on that.

Two files are the contract:

- **[The specification](../reference/specification.md)** describes the behaviour. The words MUST, SHOULD and MAY are normative.
- **[`protocol.ts`](https://github.com/offensiveadhd/reins/blob/main/packages/core/src/protocol.ts)** holds the wire types: every frame, method, error code and data shape, as types and constants with no logic. Its header says what to do when the two disagree: fix both in one change.

The specification is written to be sufficient. Every detail the test vectors depend on is written in it; no vector relies on the reference implementation for a rule the specification leaves open.

## What you might implement

You do not have to implement all three roles.

| Role | What it is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Agent** | A client: handshake, sealing, requests, events, optionally the pointer stream. | The smallest of the three. An agent in another language talks to the reference hub and drives any page connected to it. |
| **Hub** | The broker: authentication, grants, policy, rate limits, routing, the audit log. | Most of the security requirements live here. The conformance suite tests a hub from the outside. |
| **Surface** | The in-page runtime: the UI tree, command execution, consent, the indicator, the panel and the chat room. | Tied to the browser: the DOM, trusted events, a closed shadow root. |

## A sensible order

1. **Frames.** Encode and decode the ten text frames, and close with `E_BAD_FRAME` and `E_TOO_LARGE` where the specification says. See [Transports and framing](../concepts/transports-and-framing.md).
2. **The handshake.** The proof is one HMAC. Check yours against [`auth.json`](./vectors/auth.md).
3. **Sealing.** Derive the two directional keys from the transcript, MAC every message, count per direction. Check against [`seal.json`](./vectors/seal.md), including the cases that must never be sealed or opened. Then key confirmation: a sealed `ping`, a sealed `pong`.
4. **Requests and events.** Ids, the one answer per request, timeouts, the heartbeat.
5. **For an agent**: attach, then the methods you need. Apply deltas exactly: [`ui-delta.json`](./vectors/ui-delta.md).
6. **For a hub**: grants and scopes, the policy decision, rate limits and capacity, then the audit chain: [`audit.json`](./vectors/audit.md).

## What has to match exactly

Most of the protocol tolerates differences in how you build it. A few things do not, because two parties compute the same value independently:

- **Proofs and seal MACs.** Byte for byte: the contexts, the line feeds between fields, UTF-8 for everything hashed, the 32-bit big-endian lengths in the transcript hash, the 64-bit big-endian sequence number in the MAC input.
- **Canonical JSON.** Key order by UTF-16 code units, and numbers as ECMAScript writes them. The manifest digest and the audit hashes depend on it. See [`manifest.json`](./vectors/manifest.md).
- **The pointer frame.** Little-endian, with fractions rounded halves up. See [`pointer.json`](./vectors/pointer.md).
- **Delta application.** `diffNodes` and `applyOps` implement the rule of section 10, and every implementation MUST use them, or match them exactly. A different but reasonable insertion rule gives a different tree.
- **The prompt card.** It is the same wherever it is produced. An agent that renders it itself has to match character for character.
- **Merge patches.** RFC 7396, with the rule that a null property reads as absent. See [`merge-patch.json`](./vectors/merge-patch.md).
- **The policy table and the decision order.** See [`policy.json`](./vectors/policy.md).
- **How an `act` request is decided under the person's level and rules.** `decideAct` implements the order of section 12, and every surface MUST use it or match it exactly. See [`levels.json`](./vectors/levels.md).
- **Who is sent a chat message.** `chatAudience` implements the order of section 12, with the same obligation. See [`chat.json`](./vectors/chat.md).
- **The origin of a URL, and what an allowlist entry matches.** Computed by the rule of section 5, not taken from a URL library. See [`origins.json`](./vectors/origins.md).

## Conventions that bite

From the first lines of the specification:

- A size in bytes counts the UTF-8 bytes of text.
- A length in characters counts UTF-16 code units unless code points are named.
- Strings that are hashed or MACed are taken as their UTF-8 bytes.
- base64url is RFC 4648 section 5 without padding.

An implementation in a language whose strings are not UTF-16 has to count characters the way JavaScript does where the specification counts characters: the cuts of names and values, the 43 characters of a text MAC.

## The security requirements are not optional

Section 14 of the specification has 16 numbered rules an implementation MUST meet: loopback only, authenticated and sealed sessions, secrets out of URLs and logs, admission by origin and key, every forwarded request checked, the surface re-checking, schema validation before any handler, no evaluation of anything, private fields, isolated consent, human control that works without the hub, errors without internals, an audit log that fails closed, page content presented as data, levels and rules that change only on the person's input, and chat that is data and grants nothing.

The [security model](../reference/security-model.md) explains which threat each rule answers. Read its list of what Reins does not protect against as well: your implementation inherits those limits.

## Proving it

- **The vectors** are the first check, and need nothing but your own code: see [Test vectors](./test-vectors.md).
- **The hub tests** are black-box at the wire level. To run them against another hub, replace `startTestHub` in `conformance/lib/hub.ts` with code that starts that hub on a free port with the same configuration (credentials, allowed origins, policy, limits) and exposes its audit records. Tests that configure the hub through `BrokerConfig` options or read `memoryAudit` records depend on the reference configuration shape.
- **The requirements index** maps every normative sentence to the tests that check it: see [Requirements index](./requirements.md).
- **What the suite does not check** is listed, with reasons, under "Coverage limits" in [The conformance suite](./conformance-suite.md#coverage-limits).

## Versions

`challenge.v` lists what the hub speaks. The peer picks one and states it in `hello.v`. No common version is `E_VERSION`. Within a version, receivers ignore unknown fields on frames and unknown event topics, and refuse unknown methods with `E_UNKNOWN_METHOD`. From 0.2 on, an event of a kind the receiver does not know, on a topic it knows, changes nothing; a 0.2 implementation keeps to 0.1 on a link that negotiated 0.1 ([Protocol versions](../reference/protocol-versions.md), with the cases in `versions.json`).

This is protocol 0.2, which also speaks 0.1: the wire format may change before 1.0. If you are building on it, it helps to say so in the repository's issues, so that a change can take you into account: see [How to propose a protocol change](../community/protocol-changes.md).

## See it on the wire

The [playground](../../playground.html) shows every frame of a real session, on both legs: the handshake, the sealed frames with their MACs, a request as the agent sends it and as the hub forwards it, pointer frames and the credit that answers them. It is the quickest way to see what your implementation has to produce.

# Reins protocol conformance suite

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/conformance-suite.html
Section: Implementers

> What the conformance suite checks, how to run it and what it does not cover. Rendered from conformance/README.md.

This folder checks an implementation of Reins against `docs/SPEC.md` (protocol 0.2, and what it does with a peer on 0.1).
The existing tests under `packages/*/test` exercise the reference implementation's own
code paths; the tests here are written from the specification instead. Each test name
starts with the id of the requirement it checks, and `requirements.json` maps every
requirement to its spec section and its tests.

## What is here

| path | contents |
|---|---|
| `vectors/*.json` | Language-neutral test vectors: fixed inputs and expected outputs. |
| `tools/make-vectors.mjs` | Generates the vectors from the formulas in SPEC.md with `node:crypto` only. It imports nothing from `@reins/*`. |
| `vectors.test.ts` | Checks that `@reins/core` (and `verifyAuditChain` in `@reins/hub`) reproduce the vectors. |
| `hub-transport.test.ts`, `hub-handshake.test.ts`, `hub-session.test.ts`, `levels-hub.test.ts`, `chat-hub.test.ts` | Black-box hub tests. A hub is started in-process on port 0; agents and surfaces are raw `ws` sockets that build every frame, proof and seal MAC by hand (`lib/wire.ts`). `chat-hub.test.ts` covers the relay of a room's messages, their rate and their audit records (`CH-`). |
| `surface.test.ts`, `levels-surface.test.ts`, `timers-surface.test.ts`, `waiting-surface.test.ts`, `chat-surface.test.ts` | The reference driver in happy-dom, driven by a hub played with hand-built frames over an in-memory link (`lib/surface-hub.ts`). `levels-surface.test.ts` covers levels, rules, scope switches, the panel, and what a page's styles and scripts can and cannot do to the overlay (`LV-`); it reaches the panel through `shadowOf`, and plays the person with events it marks trusted. `waiting-surface.test.ts` covers what protocol 0.2 adds at the surface: requests that wait, offers at attach, a rule for a time, the rate cap, the notice after a refusal, `attention`, and the time a prompt has (`CT-`, `WT-`, `OF-`, `RT-1`, `RC-1`, `AD-1`, `AT-1`); its played hub speaks 0.2 and names each agent's version. `timers-surface.test.ts` (`LV-34`) wraps the timer functions before the driver loads, clears every timer the surface set, and shows that nothing gets looser. `chat-surface.test.ts` covers the chat methods, the room and the Chat tab (`CH-`) the same way: what the person types is a value and an input event the test marks trusted. |
| `security-hub.test.ts`, `security-surface.test.ts` | One or more tests per rule of SPEC section 14, named `S14.N ...`. Rule 14 also has a test in `mcp.test.ts`; rule 15 has its tests in `levels-surface.test.ts` and `levels-hub.test.ts`, rule 16 in `chat-surface.test.ts` and `chat-hub.test.ts`. |
| `mcp.test.ts` | The MCP adapter, spoken to with raw JSON-RPC over the SDK's in-memory transport, `reins_read` (`MCP-6`) and `reins_chat` included (`CH-15`), the one rule for text a page supplied (`MCP-7`, `MCP-8`), the hand-over of chat messages over the shell session (`CH-28`), and the `chat-serve` runner with a command that echoes what it is given (`CH-16`) and with one that leaves a process running (`CH-29`). |
| `hub-transport.test.ts`, `hub-handshake.test.ts`, `hub-session.test.ts` | Black-box hub tests. A hub is started in-process on port 0; agents and surfaces are raw `ws` sockets that build every frame, proof and seal MAC by hand (`lib/wire.ts`). |
| `surface.test.ts` | The reference driver in happy-dom, driven by a hub played with hand-built frames over an in-memory link (`lib/surface-hub.ts`). |
| `security-hub.test.ts`, `security-surface.test.ts` | One or more tests per rule of SPEC section 14, named `S14.N ...`. Rule 14 also has a test in `mcp.test.ts`. |
| `mcp.test.ts` | The MCP adapter, spoken to with raw JSON-RPC over the SDK's in-memory transport. |
| `waiting-hub.test.ts` | Sections 6, 13 and 16 at the hub (`WH-`): requests that wait, with the SDK as the agent and a raw socket as a 0.1 agent, against the real hub and a played surface that keeps a waiting list; the ticket a hub refuses, the answer it relays, the attach it withdraws, and the hub's half of the consent-timeout change (`WH-8`). |
| `versions.test.ts`, `versions-surface.test.ts` | Section 16 (`VER-6` to `VER-14`). A peer on 0.1 is a raw socket that names `0.1` in its hello and records every frame it is sent, so what the hub must not send it is checked on the wire; the agent SDK is run against a hub that lists 0.1 alone (`versions: ["0.1"]`), and the driver against a played hub whose challenge lists 0.1 alone. The `versions.json` vectors are checked here too (`VEC-VERSIONS`). |
| `origins.test.ts` | Section 5, "Origins": the origin vectors against `@reins/core`, and surfaces and agents from `file://`, app origins and `null` on raw sockets. |
| `electron.test.ts` | The Electron port of section 3 and `reins-electron` of section 15. Electron is played by the stand-ins in `lib/electron.ts`: no Electron is installed or started. |
| `electron-page.test.ts` | How long the driver of an adopted page lives: the real page glue and driver in happy-dom, against the real injector and broker, with the browser between them played by `lib/electron.ts`. |
| `requirements.json` | `{ id, section, text, quotes?, tests }` per requirement. `quotes` are exact substrings of the MUST / MUST NOT / SHALL sentences an entry covers. |
| `requirements.test.ts` | Fails if a normative sentence or a section 14 rule has no entry, if a quote no longer occurs in the spec, or if an entry names a test that does not exist. |
| `lib/` | Helpers: the raw wire client, hub and surface harnesses, an independent canonical-JSON function, and the spec and test-name extractors used by the meta-test. |

## Running

```
npm run test:conformance
```

This runs `vitest run conformance`. No build step is needed: `vitest.config.ts` maps the
`@reins/*` imports to the package sources. Every hub listens on port 0 and every temporary
file goes under the OS temp directory, so the suite can run next to a hub on port 7346.
A full run takes about half a minute; three tests wait out the hub's 5 s timers on purpose
(HS-9, HS-17) or create 64 connections (CAP-2).

To regenerate the vectors after a spec change:

```
node conformance/tools/make-vectors.mjs          # write vectors/*.json
node conformance/tools/make-vectors.mjs --check  # exit 1 if a file would change
```

`node conformance/lib/spec-text.mjs` prints the normative sentences and section 14 rules
the meta-test reads from SPEC.md; `node conformance/lib/test-names.mjs` prints the test
titles it knows.

## Using the vectors from another implementation

Each file in `vectors/` is self-describing: `spec` names the section, `formula` or
`layout` restates the rule, and `note` explains the cases. Every detail the vectors depend
on is now written in SPEC.md; no vector relies on the reference implementation for a rule
the spec leaves open. Byte strings are hex, base64url values are unpadded (RFC 4648
section 5).

| file | how to use it |
|---|---|
| `auth.json` | For each case compute `HMAC-SHA256(key, peerInput)` and `HMAC-SHA256(key, hubInput)` over UTF-8 bytes, base64url; compare with `peerProof` and `hubProof`. The third case has a non-ASCII kid. |
| `seal.json` | Derive `th`, `kPeer` and `kHub` from `key`, `nonce`, `cnonce`, `challengeText`, `helloText`, `welcomeText`; seal the `peerToHub` messages in order from sequence 0 and compare with `wire` / `wireHex`; do the same with `hubToPeer`; open the wire messages and expect the payloads. `macOnly` gives MACs at large sequence numbers. `illFormed` must never be sealed or opened. |
| `pointer.json` | Encode `frame` and compare with `hex`; decode `hex` and compare with `frame`; `clamp` and `rounding` cases check the encoding of fractions and `dt`; `invalid` must be refused. |
| `merge-patch.json` | `apply`: RFC 7396 appendix A. `diff`: any patch P with apply(from, P) == to passes. `equal`: no patch at all; some cases differ only in null properties, which read as absent. |
| `ui-delta.json` | `apply`: apply `ops` to `nodes`, expect `expect`. `diff`: your diff, applied to `prev`, must give `next`, with every `del` first. `render`: the compact tree text and single node lines. `renderDelta`: delta text rendered against `prev`. |
| `methods.json` | Method to scope table, `HUB_METHODS`, `READ_ONLY_METHODS`, `CHAT_SPEAK_METHODS`, scope intersection. |
| `policy.json` | Profile table with its defaults (levels, panel and `chatRelay` included), override precedence, strictness order. |
| `levels.json` | `rows`: split each row on spaces into `columns`; from the policy decision, the action's risk, the level, the rule (`-` for none) and the levels on offer (joined by `+`), your decision for an `act` request must give `outcome`, and `by` and `remember` where they are not `-`. `c1`: a request with c:1 counts as the decision in `counts`. `offered`: the levels on offer from the two `human.levels` lists (`strict` and `ask` always). `hub`: the hub's decision for an action as a surface reads it from `decisions` in attach; anything missing or malformed is `confirm`. `allowRule`: where the rule allow may be set. |
| `chat.json` | `text.cases`: trim the text (`unit` and `times` stand for a repeated unit between `before` and `after`); with `ok` it is kept and has `length`, otherwise `chat.say` answers `E_BAD_ARGS`. `statusNote.cases`: the note as it is kept, or refused. `message`: take the `valid` messages, keeping only `fields`, and drop the `invalid` ones. `audience.rows`: split each row on spaces into `columns`; from the agents in the room, the agents among them that hear each other, who speaks and whom they address (`person` for the person alone), your decision must give `outcome` and `result`. `relay`: the three values of `chatRelay`, and for every pair the stricter one. `auditDigest`: the canonical JSON and the unkeyed digest a chat text is recorded with, whatever else was sent with it. `lines`: a chat text as the `| ` lines a model is handed, and a session id as it is printed. |
| `manifest.json` | Canonical JSON (with `canonicalCases` for key order and numbers) and digest of a manifest, and the prompt card of SPEC section 7. |
| `audit.json` | An unkeyed and a keyed audit chain to verify; `args` is SHA-256, or HMAC under the key, of `argsCanonical`. |
| `errors.json`, `limits.json` | The complete error code list of SPEC section 6, and numeric limits the spec states. |
| `origins.json` | `urlOrigin`: the origin of each `url` (JSON null: not a URL; the string `"null"`: opaque). `allowed`: whether `entries` admit `origin`. `surfaceUrl`: whether `url` may be `hello.surface.url` on a connection from `origin`. |

The hub tests in `hub-*.test.ts` are black-box at the wire level: to run them against
another hub, replace `startTestHub` in `lib/hub.ts` with code that starts that hub on a
free port with the same configuration (credentials, allowed origins, policy, limits) and
exposes its audit records. Tests that configure the hub through `BrokerConfig` options or
read `memoryAudit` records depend on the reference configuration shape.

## Coverage limits

These requirements are not checked, or only partly:

- TR-2 (refuse a non-loopback remote address): needs a second network interface; the test
  only shows loopback clients are served.
- Section 16: no implementation of protocol 0.1 is run. A peer on 0.1 is a raw socket that
  names `0.1` in its hello, and a hub on 0.1 is the reference hub told to list 0.1 alone,
  or a played one. That the agent SDK drops an event 0.1 does not have when a 0.1 hub
  relays one is covered in `packages/agent/test/agent.test.ts`, not here.
- S14.3, owner-only files: checked by POSIX mode only; on Windows the ACL is not inspected
  (the test is skipped there). The token file written by the CLI is not covered.
- Section 5: the inbound bound before authentication (16 messages, 64 KiB) and dropping
  what a peer sends after a failed proof race the hub's asynchronous proof check, so
  they are not tested at the wire; the link bound (4096 messages, 16 MiB) is not covered.
- Section 11 drop policy (droppable frames above 256 KiB of surface backlog, stall at
  1 MiB), receiver playback, coalescing on the sender, and Pause and Stop discarding
  queued points: need control of socket buffers or animation frames; only
  `playbackRate` and the credit batching are checked.
- Section 9 ordering, command batching per animation frame (6 ms), cursor glide timing,
  and "checks hold across waits": timing-dependent, not covered.
- Section 12: the 500 ms arming of Allow, Allow waiting for a tall card to be scrolled,
  the escaping of invisible code points on the card, the "Request withdrawn" notice, the
  indicator above the prompt's backdrop or inside a modal dialog or fullscreen element,
  and `human.yieldMs` after real input (happy-dom input is never trusted): not covered
  beyond what S14.10 and S14.11 check.
- Section 12, the panel: happy-dom has no layout and no trusted input. The `LV-` surface
  tests mark their own events as trusted to play the person, so they show that unmarked
  events do nothing, not that a browser marks events correctly. Where the panel sits (beside
  a consent card on a wide viewport, under its backdrop on a narrow one, inside a modal
  dialog or a fullscreen element), the "Always allow" step on a card and the colours of the
  indicator are not covered here; the driver's own tests
  (`packages/driver/test/levels.test.ts`) cover their logic.
- Section 12, the overlay and the page: happy-dom has no top layer, no painting, no native
  `isTrusted` and no IntersectionObserver. `LV-24` to `LV-26` check the stylesheet's text,
  the effects a style engine reports on an ancestor of the host, and that a late hook is
  handed no listener. `LV-29` plays keys as events it marks trusted and moves the focus
  itself, since happy-dom does not move it on Tab; `LV-32` reads `zoom` from a computed
  style it sets, and `LV-35` uses a stand-in for the Popover API. That page CSS leaves every pixel of the overlay as it was, that the
  host is last in the top layer (also above a page's own popover and inside a modal dialog),
  that a forged or borrowed event moves nothing where the browser's own getter is read,
  where a real key or click lands (Tab and Enter typed for the page, a word and Enter,
  Tab, Enter, Tab, Enter), that `::before`, `::after`, `::marker` and `::first-letter`
  rules of the page add no box to the host, and that `zoom` and `display: none` on `html`
  stop commands, is checked in a real Chromium by
  `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` (`npm run test:browser`; it skips when no Chromium is
  found unless `--require` is given). The driver's `packages/driver/test/hardening.test.ts`
  covers the logic of the top layer and of the visibility observer with stand-ins.
- Section 12, chat: happy-dom has no layout and no trusted input. The `CH-` surface tests
  set the composer's value and mark their own input, key and click events as trusted to
  play the person, so they show that unmarked events and a value set by script send
  nothing, not that a browser marks events correctly or that an input method behaves.
  How the tab looks (light and dark, a narrow viewport), the scroll position of the
  transcript, the lapse of a status after 2 minutes, what a screen reader says, and the
  focus that returns to the composer after a command are not covered here; the driver's
  own tests (`packages/driver/test/chat.test.ts`) cover the logic of the last two. That a
  page's own script can read the composer and the transcript and alter what is sent
  (`docs/SECURITY.md`, "What Reins does not protect against") is stated, not tested: the
  tests show what an agent cannot do, and that ordinary bubbling listeners see nothing.
  That the composer takes no input while an app action runs is tested with an action
  that writes into the field, not with a browser's `execCommand`.
- Section 13: fail-closed on more than 1000 queued records, `lost` summaries, a peer
  closed for not reading, refusing to continue a log whose chain or head does not
  verify (`fileAudit`), and the 32-agent cap.
- Sections 3 and 15, Electron: nothing here starts Electron. What Chromium sends as
  `Origin`, the port crossing `contextIsolation`, the debugging pipe, the driver in a world
  of its own under a page's Content Security Policy, and consent, the panel, a level and
  the chat in a real window with real input are checked by `npm run test:electron`, which
  is not part of this suite (see `docs/ELECTRON.md`).
- Section 15: CLI behaviour (token files, secret-file checks, flags, escaping of page
  text), the `[unverified hub data]` marking of the MCP adapter, and the agent SDK beyond
  its pointer credit are not covered. Of `reins_chat`, the 150 s cap of a wait is checked
  as a constant and with a mock clock in `packages/mcp/test/chat.test.ts`, not by waiting.
  The read of the room every 45 s while a wait is in flight is tested there too, and
  against a real hub whose clock is moved in `examples/kiosk/test/chat.test.ts`.
  Of `chat-serve`, the command line, the timeout and the failure notices are covered in
  `packages/mcp/test/chat-serve.test.ts`, not here. `CH-29` shows here, on the machine the
  tests run on, that a process a command left running when it exited is ended. What a
  Windows job object holds beyond that (a process whose parent has exited, a tree that
  goes on growing, one started by cmd.exe, PowerShell or Python, a request to leave the
  job refused) and that nothing is run where no job object can be made, is covered by the
  tests named `review round 2, F3` in that file, on Windows only; the process-group path
  is covered by the tests there that are not Windows-only, on the machine they run on.
  That `down` and `up` leave the process of a stale announcement alone, that `up` prints
  the hub's origin warnings, and that an option a running session cannot take is refused,
  are covered in `packages/mcp/test/shell.test.ts`; what a system reports as a process's
  creation time is asked for real only on the machine the tests run on. No test runs a model, and none runs a
  harness: the Claude Code subagent in `integrations/` was not run under Claude Code.

Tests marked `it.fails` are places where the implementation does not do what the spec
says; each carries a `// SPEC MISMATCH:` comment.

## Requirements

| id | section | what is checked | tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-1 | 3 | The hub binds loopback addresses only and refuses any other bind address. | TR-1 |
| TR-2 | 3 | The hub rejects a socket whose remote address is not loopback. | TR-2 |
| TR-3 | 3 | The hub rejects a Host header other than 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] with its port. | S14.1 |
| TR-4 | 3 | The hub requires the reins.v1 subprotocol. | TR-4 |
| TR-5 | 3 | The hub disables per-message compression. | TR-5 |
| TR-6 | 3 | The hub answers plain HTTP with a bare status and no body. | TR-6 |
| FR-1 | 4 | A receiver closes with E_TOO_LARGE on an oversize frame and with E_BAD_FRAME on invalid JSON, an unknown t or a missing field; closing with a code is bye {code} then close, and a message the transport cannot take is closed with WebSocket code 1009. | FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, HS-8 |
| FR-2 | 4 | The hub announces its limits in welcome; defaults are 256 KiB text, 16 KiB binary, heartbeatMs 15000, reqTimeoutMs 15000, consentTimeoutMs 60000. | FR-4, VEC-LIMITS |
| HS-1 | 5 | The hub sends challenge {v, nonce, hub} first; nonces are 32 fresh random bytes, base64url. | HS-1 |
| HS-2 | 5 | Proofs are base64url HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the context, role, kid, nonce and cnonce joined by line feeds, keyed by the UTF-8 bytes of the secret, with the contexts reins.v1.auth and reins.v1.hub. | HS-2, VEC-AUTH |
| HS-3 | 5 | A failed hello is answered with bye E_AUTH and closed. | HS-3 |
| HS-4 | 5 | Agents must authenticate. | HS-4, S14.2 |
| HS-5 | 5 | A failed proof is answered after 200 ms, doubling per failure in the last minute, up to 3 s; a correct proof is never refused because others failed. | HS-5, HS-6 |
| HS-6 | 5 | At most 16 handshakes are pending; further connections get E_BUSY. | HS-7 |
| HS-7 | 5 | A peer that sends anything but hello first, or takes longer than 5 s, is closed. | HS-8, HS-9 |
| HS-8 | 5 | Keys shorter than 32 characters are rejected. | HS-10 |
| HS-9 | 5 | A peer that holds a key verifies welcome.proof and closes on mismatch. | HS-11 |

# Test vectors

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/test-vectors.html
Section: Implementers

> Language-neutral test vectors for the parts of the protocol that two implementations have to compute identically. Fixed inputs and expected outputs, browsable here and downloadable as JSON.

## What they are

The conformance suite includes language-neutral test vectors: fixed inputs and expected outputs for authentication proofs, sealed frames, the pointer frame layout, deltas, policy decisions and more. They were computed independently of the reference implementation, for anyone writing another one.

`conformance/tools/make-vectors.mjs` generates them from the formulas in the specification with `node:crypto` only. It imports nothing from the reference packages. The suite then checks that the reference implementation reproduces them.

## The files

There are 16 files. Each has a page here that shows its content, and each can be downloaded as it is in the repository.

| file | what it holds | covers |
|---|---|---|
| [`audit.json`](./vectors/audit.md) | Audit hash chain | SPEC.md section 13, "Audit" |
| [`auth.json`](./vectors/auth.md) | Handshake authentication proofs | SPEC.md section 5 |
| [`chat.json`](./vectors/chat.md) | Chat: texts, messages and who hears them | SPEC.md section 9 (chat.say, chat.read, chat.status), section 12 ("Chat") and section 13 ("Chat relay") |
| [`consent.json`](./vectors/consent.md) | Consent in protocol 0.2: requests that wait, offers at attach, a rule for a time, the rate cap | SPEC.md section 12 ("Requests that wait", "Offers at attach", "Levels and rules": a rule for a time and the rate cap) and the section 12 table |
| [`errors.json`](./vectors/errors.md) | Error codes | SPEC.md section 6 (the table of codes) and sections 4 to 16 |
| [`levels.json`](./vectors/levels.md) | Levels, rules and the decision for an act request | SPEC.md section 12, "Levels and rules" |
| [`limits.json`](./vectors/limits.md) | Default limits and fixed numbers | SPEC.md sections 3 to 13 |
| [`manifest.json`](./vectors/manifest.md) | Manifest digest and prompt card | SPEC.md section 7 |
| [`merge-patch.json`](./vectors/merge-patch.md) | JSON merge patch for state events | SPEC.md section 10 ("an RFC 7396 merge patch"); RFC 7396 section 2 and appendix A |
| [`methods.json`](./vectors/methods.md) | Agent methods, their scopes, and which take a surface id | SPEC.md section 9 table; section 6 (hub methods); section 8 (scope order) |
| [`origins.json`](./vectors/origins.md) | Origins: of a URL, in an allowlist, of hello.surface.url | SPEC.md section 5, "Origins" |
| [`pointer.json`](./vectors/pointer.md) | Binary pointer frames | SPEC.md section 11, "Pointer stream" (layout table and encoding of fractions) |
| [`policy.json`](./vectors/policy.md) | Policy profiles and action decisions | SPEC.md section 12 table and "Action decisions"; strictness allow < confirm < deny (section 12 "Two enforcement points": the stricter decision) |
| [`seal.json`](./vectors/seal.md) | Sealed-session keys and frame MACs | SPEC.md section 5, "Sealed sessions" |
| [`ui-delta.json`](./vectors/ui-delta.md) | UI-tree delta operations | SPEC.md section 10, "Applying a delta" and "Text rendering" |
| [`versions.json`](./vectors/versions.md) | Protocol versions and what a link on 0.1 leaves out | SPEC.md section 16 |

Each file is self-describing: `spec` names the section, `formula`, `layout` or `rule` restates the rule, and `note` explains the cases. Byte strings are hex, and base64url values are unpadded (RFC 4648 section 5).

## How to use them

| file | how to use it |
|---|---|
| `auth.json` | For each case compute `HMAC-SHA256(key, peerInput)` and `HMAC-SHA256(key, hubInput)` over UTF-8 bytes, base64url; compare with `peerProof` and `hubProof`. The third case has a non-ASCII kid. |
| `seal.json` | Derive `th`, `kPeer` and `kHub` from `key`, `nonce`, `cnonce`, `challengeText`, `helloText`, `welcomeText`; seal the `peerToHub` messages in order from sequence 0 and compare with `wire` / `wireHex`; do the same with `hubToPeer`; open the wire messages and expect the payloads. `macOnly` gives MACs at large sequence numbers. `illFormed` must never be sealed or opened. |
| `pointer.json` | Encode `frame` and compare with `hex`; decode `hex` and compare with `frame`; `clamp` and `rounding` cases check the encoding of fractions and `dt`; `invalid` must be refused. |
| `merge-patch.json` | `apply`: RFC 7396 appendix A. `diff`: any patch P with apply(from, P) == to passes. `equal`: no patch at all; some cases differ only in null properties, which read as absent. |
| `ui-delta.json` | `apply`: apply `ops` to `nodes`, expect `expect`. `diff`: your diff, applied to `prev`, must give `next`, with every `del` first. `render`: the compact tree text and single node lines. `renderDelta`: delta text rendered against `prev`. |
| `methods.json` | Method to scope table, `HUB_METHODS`, `READ_ONLY_METHODS`, `CHAT_SPEAK_METHODS`, scope intersection. |
| `policy.json` | Profile table with its defaults (levels, panel and `chatRelay` included), override precedence, strictness order. |
| `levels.json` | `rows`: split each row on spaces into `columns`; from the policy decision, the action's risk, the level, the rule (`-` for none) and the levels on offer (joined by `+`), your decision for an `act` request must give `outcome`, and `by` and `remember` where they are not `-`. `c1`: a request with c:1 counts as the decision in `counts`. `offered`: the levels on offer from the two `human.levels` lists (`strict` and `ask` always). `hub`: the hub's decision for an action as a surface reads it from `decisions` in attach; anything missing or malformed is `confirm`. `allowRule`: where the rule allow may be set. |
| `chat.json` | `text.cases`: trim the text (`unit` and `times` stand for a repeated unit between `before` and `after`); with `ok` it is kept and has `length`, otherwise `chat.say` answers `E_BAD_ARGS`. `statusNote.cases`: the note as it is kept, or refused. `message`: take the `valid` messages, keeping only `fields`, and drop the `invalid` ones. `audience.rows`: split each row on spaces into `columns`; from the agents in the room, the agents among them that hear each other, who speaks and whom they address (`person` for the person alone), your decision must give `outcome` and `result`. `relay`: the three values of `chatRelay`, and for every pair the stricter one. `auditDigest`: the canonical JSON and the unkeyed digest a chat text is recorded with, whatever else was sent with it. `lines`: a chat text as the `| ` lines a model is handed, and a session id as it is printed. |
| `manifest.json` | Canonical JSON (with `canonicalCases` for key order and numbers) and digest of a manifest, and the prompt card of SPEC section 7. |
| `audit.json` | An unkeyed and a keyed audit chain to verify; `args` is SHA-256, or HMAC under the key, of `argsCanonical`. |
| `errors.json`, `limits.json` | The complete error code list of SPEC section 6, and numeric limits the spec states. |
| `origins.json` | `urlOrigin`: the origin of each `url` (JSON null: not a URL; the string `"null"`: opaque). `allowed`: whether `entries` admit `origin`. `surfaceUrl`: whether `url` may be `hello.surface.url` on a connection from `origin`. |

Start with `auth.json` and `seal.json`. An implementation that reproduces those two has the proofs and the frame MACs right, which is what a handshake and a sealed session with the reference hub rest on.

## Regenerating

After a change to the specification:

```bash
node conformance/tools/make-vectors.mjs          # write vectors/*.json
node conformance/tools/make-vectors.mjs --check  # exit 1 if a file would change
```

The pages here are built from the files in the repository, so they always show what the suite checks.

## Further reading

- [Writing another implementation](./writing-an-implementation.md)
- [The conformance suite](./conformance-suite.md)
- [Requirements index](./requirements.md)
