# Binary pointer frames

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/vectors/pointer.html
Section: Implementers

> Test vectors: Binary pointer frames. Shown here as it is in conformance/vectors/pointer.json.

Protocol `0.2`. Covers: SPEC.md section 11, "Pointer stream" (layout table and encoding of fractions).

[Download pointer.json](./pointer.json): the file itself, as the conformance suite reads it.

## How to use it

Encode `frame` and compare with `hex`; decode `hex` and compare with `frame`; `clamp` and `rounding` cases check the encoding of fractions and `dt`; `invalid` must be refused.

## Layout

```text
offset 0  u8   kind  0x01 (BIN_POINTER)
offset 1  u8   flags 0x01 PTR_FLAG_DROPPABLE, 0x02 PTR_FLAG_END
offset 2  u16  ch
offset 4  u32  seq of the first point
offset 8  u16  n, number of points
offset 10 n x { u16 x, u16 y, u16 dt }, all little-endian
a fraction f is sent as round(f x 65535) after clamping to 0..1 (non-finite as 0), halves up; read back as u / 65535; dt is rounded and clamped to 0..65535
```

## Notes

The layout and the rounding rule are in SPEC 11. `cases` use exact multiples of 1/65535; `rounding` checks fractions between two steps; `clamp` checks out-of-range values; `invalid` frames are not pointer frames.

## cases

4 cases.

```json
[
  {
    "name": "one point, no flags",
    "frame": {
      "ch": 1,
      "seq": 0,
      "flags": 0,
      "points": [

          "x": 0,
          "y": 1,
          "dt": 0
        }
      ]
    },
    "hex": "010001000000000001000000ffff0000"
  },
  {
    "name": "three points, droppable",
    "frame": {
      "ch": 7,
      "seq": 1000,
      "flags": 1,
      "points": [
        {
          "x": 0.000015259021896696422,
          "y": 0.000030518043793392844,
          "dt": 16
        },
```

# Policy profiles and action decisions

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/vectors/policy.html
Section: Implementers

> Test vectors: Policy profiles and action decisions. Shown here as it is in conformance/vectors/policy.json.

Protocol `0.2`. Covers: SPEC.md section 12 table and "Action decisions"; strictness allow < confirm < deny (section 12 "Two enforcement points": the stricter decision).

[Download policy.json](./policy.json): the file itself, as the conformance suite reads it.

## How to use it

Profile table with its defaults (levels, panel and `chatRelay` included), override precedence, strictness order.

## Notes

"navigation: same origin" is checked as a non-empty nav prefix list that admits a same-origin path; "off" as an empty list. "user controls" maps to human.pause and human.stop. "levels the person may set" is human.levels as listed (kiosk lists none, and has no panel in which to choose one: its grants stay at ask) and "the indicator opens the panel" is human.panel. "a page inside a frame: refused" is framed == false. "agents hear each other in the chat" is chatRelay: `on` (always), `person` (once the person switches it on in the Chat tab) or `off` (never). The kiosk attach entry "allow, with a provisioned agent" is checked as attach == allow. `defaults` are the remaining rows of the table, in Policy field names and milliseconds.

# Sealed-session keys and frame MACs

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/vectors/seal.html
Section: Implementers

> Test vectors: Sealed-session keys and frame MACs. Shown here as it is in conformance/vectors/seal.json.

Protocol `0.2`. Covers: SPEC.md section 5, "Sealed sessions".

[Download seal.json](./seal.json): the file itself, as the conformance suite reads it.

## How to use it

Derive `th`, `kPeer` and `kHub` from `key`, `nonce`, `cnonce`, `challengeText`, `helloText`, `welcomeText`; seal the `peerToHub` messages in order from sequence 0 and compare with `wire` / `wireHex`; do the same with `hubToPeer`; open the wire messages and expect the payloads. `macOnly` gives MACs at large sequence numbers. `illFormed` must never be sealed or opened.

## Formula

```text
th = b64url(SHA-256(L(c) || c || L(h) || h || L(w) || w)), with c, h, w the UTF-8 bytes of challengeText, helloText, welcomeText and L(x) the byte length of x as an unsigned 32-bit big-endian integer
k = HMAC-SHA256(key, context + "\n" + nonce + "\n" + cnonce + "\n" + th), context "reins.v1.seal.peer" (peer sends) or "reins.v1.seal.hub" (hub sends)
mac = HMAC-SHA256(k, u64be(seq) || kind || payload), kind 0x74 text, 0x62 binary; seq counts from 0 per direction and is never sent
sealed text = b64url(mac) + "." + text; sealed binary = bytes || mac
```

## Notes

Everything here is stated in SPEC 5: the HMAC key and message are UTF-8 bytes, th is base64url text, k is the raw 32-byte HMAC output used as the key of the frame MAC, and the payload of a text message is its UTF-8 bytes. `macOnly` entries use sequence numbers that the public API cannot reach (the counter starts at 0 and is internal); they are here for other implementations. `illFormed` is a text with a lone surrogate (written as a JSON escape), which must never be sealed or opened.

## Fixed values

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `key` | `HebNZMN9EImpyoAZxAMca3WUyq-yG5DAkpSIfXpS294` |
| `nonce` | `X4jwsNU4ZbyLfcfpTAjqL6YTHwJFRJnhOkaAiob2bbU` |
| `cnonce` | `WI8VBFzQHSRrn0GqeV7pEYkNsGcnJACIX8XysTe0wuc` |
| `challengeText` | `{"t":"challenge","v":["0.1"],"nonce":"X4jwsNU4ZbyLfcfpTAjqL6YTHwJFRJnhOkaAiob2bbU","hub":{"name":"conformance-hub","ver":"0.1.0"}}` |
| `helloText` | `{"t":"hello","v":"0.1","role":"agent","name":"conformance","cnonce":"WI8VBFzQHSRrn0GqeV7pEYkNsGcnJACIX8XysTe0wuc","auth":{"kid":"default","proof":"nD89mHMkpZjv1bORaBzPNGoMXilSlR-6cu-JIzNjpZs"}}` |
| `welcomeText` | `{"t":"welcome","v":"0.1","session":"a1","role":"agent","limits":{"maxText":262144,"maxBinary":16384,"heartbeatMs":15000,"reqTimeoutMs":15000,"consentTimeoutMs":60000},"proof":"BYpxxhfA4x9Xak04Rvey74cSQOaBtXiYKY7E3A7N3R0"}` |
| `th` | `2F9jYemeRLbGr6ALI0IOJOPEIXO3o41FVekTBjdE1TI` |

# UI-tree delta operations

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/vectors/ui-delta.html
Section: Implementers

> Test vectors: UI-tree delta operations. Shown here as it is in conformance/vectors/ui-delta.json.

Protocol `0.2`. Covers: SPEC.md section 10, "Applying a delta" and "Text rendering".

[Download ui-delta.json](./ui-delta.json): the file itself, as the conformance suite reads it.

## How to use it

`apply`: apply `ops` to `nodes`, expect `expect`. `diff`: your diff, applied to `prev`, must give `next`, with every `del` first. `render`: the compact tree text and single node lines. `renderDelta`: delta text rendered against `prev`.

## Rule

```text
Ops apply in order. A set whose handle is in the tree replaces that node in place. A set with a new handle is inserted right after the node of the preceding op when that op was a set, and at the front of the list otherwise. A del removes the node with its handle and does nothing when there is none.
```

## Notes

`apply` cases follow the rule literally, including a del of an absent handle. `diff` cases give (prev, next) pairs: any op list made of set and del, with every del before the first set, that turns prev into next is accepted, since the choice of moved nodes (a longest run of survivors in their old order) can tie. `render` is the node-line example of section 10; `renderDelta` gives delta texts rendered against the tree they apply to.

# Protocol versions and what a link on 0.1 leaves out

Page: https://reins.offensiveadhd.com/wiki/implementers/vectors/versions.html
Section: Implementers

> Test vectors: Protocol versions and what a link on 0.1 leaves out. Shown here as it is in conformance/vectors/versions.json.

Protocol `0.2`. Covers: SPEC.md section 16.

[Download versions.json](./versions.json): the file itself, as the conformance suite reads it.

## Notes

`versions` is what an implementation of this document lists in challenge.v, newest first. `pick`: the version a peer names in hello, null where the handshake ends with E_VERSION. `v01` is what 0.1 has, `added` what 0.2 added to it. `events`, `methods`, `scopes` and `errors` say what exists on a link by the version it negotiated: an implementation of 0.2 neither sends nor takes the rest on a 0.1 link.

## versions

```json
[
  "0.2",
  "0.1"
]
```
